SideSetArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the of all the elements in a file as sets in their own right. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per side. For example, a hexahedron has 18 sides: 6 faces and 12 edges. Any of these sides may be individually called out in a set and assigned a result value. The accompanying SideSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
SideSetArrayStatus.label: Side Set Array Status

SideSetResultArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the of all the elements in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per side. For example, a hexahedron has 18 sides: 6 faces and 12 edges. Any of these sides may be individually called out in a set and assigned a result value. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the SideSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
SideSetResultArrayStatus.label: Side Set Result Array Status

UseLegacyBlockNamesWithElementTypes.description: In previous versions, the reader added the type of elements in the block to the block name when no name was provided for the block. This has issues with consistency when naming blocks across ranks for partitioned files. Hence we no longer do that. For legacy pipelines, one can enable the old behavior by setting this flag to true.
UseLegacyBlockNamesWithElementTypes.label: Use Legacy Block Names With Element Types

XMLFileName.description: This property specifies the name of an XML file containing part and material descriptions and a mapping to element blocks.
XMLFileName.label: XML File Name

filters/ExtractHierarchicalDataSets.long: This filter extracts a list of datasets from hierarchical datasets.
filters/ExtractHierarchicalDataSets.description: This filter extracts a list of datasets from hierarchical datasets.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Extract Datasets filter.
Input.label: Input

SelectedDataSets.description: Specify a pair, level and dataset index, for every dataset from the input AMR dataset to extract.
SelectedDataSets.label: Selected Data Sets

filters/AttributeDataToTableFilter.short: Extract attribute data as a table.
filters/AttributeDataToTableFilter.long: Extract attribute data as a table.
filters/AttributeDataToTableFilter.description: This is a filter that produces a vtkTable from the chosen attribute in the input data object. This filter can accept composite datasets. If the input is a composite dataset, the output is a multiblock with vtkTable leaves.
filters/AttributeDataToTableFilter.selection: Extract attribute data as a table.

AddMetaData.description: It is possible for this filter to add additional meta-data to the field data such as point coordinates (when point attributes are selected and input is pointset) or structured coordinates etc. To enable this addition of extra information, turn this flag on. Off by default.
AddMetaData.label: Add Meta Data

FieldAssociation.description: Select the attribute data to pass.
FieldAssociation.label: Field Association

Input.description: This property specifies the input of the filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/ExtractBlock.long: Extract chosen blocks from composite datasets
filters/ExtractBlock.description: Extract selected blocks from a composite dataset.

Assembly.description: Select which assembly is used when specify selectors to choose blocks to extract.
Assembly.label: Assembly

Input.description: Specify the input to this filter.
Input.label: Input

Selectors.description: Sepecify the selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to extract from the input dataset.
Selectors.label: Selectors

filters/CTHPart.short: Extract a part from a CTH dataset.
filters/CTHPart.long: Create a surface from a CTH volume fraction.
filters/CTHPart.description: Extract CTH Parts is a specialized filter for visualizing the data from a CTH simulation. It first converts the selected cell-centered arrays to point-centered ones. It then contours each array at a value of 0.5. The user has the option of clipping the resulting surface(s) with a plane. This filter only operates on unstructured data. It produces polygonal output.
filters/CTHPart.selection: Extract a part from a CTH dataset.

CapSurfaces.description: When enabled, volume surfaces are capped to produce visually closed surface.
CapSurfaces.label: Cap Surfaces

ClipPlane.description: This property specifies whether to clip the dataset, and if so, it also specifies the parameters of the plane with which to clip.
ClipPlane.label: Clip Type

GenerateSolidGeometry.description: Generate solid output with 3D cells. When set to false, 2D contours are generated.
GenerateSolidGeometry.label: Generate Solid Geometry

GenerateTriangles.description: Triangulate results. When set to false, the internal cut and contour filters are told not to triangulate results if possible.
GenerateTriangles.label: Generate Triangles

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Extract CTH Parts filter.
Input.label: Input

RemoveGhostCells.description: When set to false, the output surfaces will not hide contours extracted from ghost cells. This results in overlapping contours but overcomes holes. Default is set to true.
RemoveGhostCells.label: Remove Ghost Cells

VolumeArrays.description: This property specifies the name(s) of the volume fraction array(s) for generating parts.
VolumeArrays.label: Volume Arrays

VolumeFractionSurfaceValue.description: The value of this property is the volume fraction value for the surface.
VolumeFractionSurfaceValue.label: Volume Fraction Value

filters/ExtractCellsAlongLine.description: This filter extract the cells intersected by a line.

Point1.description: This property controls the coordinates of the first endpoint of the line.
Point1.label: Point1

Point2.description: This property controls the coordinates of the second endpoint of the line.
Point2.label: Point2

filters/ExtractCellsAlongLineCustom.short: Extract cells along input lines from custom source
filters/ExtractCellsAlongLineCustom.description: The Extract Cells Along Lines From Custom Source filter extracts cells from the input data set that intersect lines from a custom source. This source can be either an Unstructured Grid or a Poly Data. Any cells other than lines or poly lines are ignored in the source.
filters/ExtractCellsAlongLineCustom.selection: Extract cells along input lines from custom source

Source.description: This property specifies the dataset composed of the lines and poly lines used to extract cells in the input.
Source.label: Source

filters/ExtractGeometry.short: Extract cells that are inside/outside a region or at a region boundary.
filters/ExtractGeometry.long: This filter extracts cells that are inside/outside a region or at a region boundary.
filters/ExtractGeometry.description: This filter extracts from its input dataset all cells that are either completely inside or outside of a specified region (implicit function). On output, the filter generates an unstructured grid. To use this filter you must specify a region (implicit function). You must also specify whether to extract cells lying inside or outside of the region. An option exists to extract cells that are neither inside or outside (i.e., boundary).
filters/ExtractGeometry.selection: Extract cells that are inside/outside a region or at a region boundary.

Extract intersected.description: This parameter controls whether to extract cells that are on the boundary of the region.
Extract intersected.label: Extract intersected

Extract only intersected.description: This parameter controls whether to extract only cells that are on the boundary of the region. If this parameter is set, the Extraction Side parameter is ignored. If Extract Intersected is off, this parameter has no effect.
Extract only intersected.label: Extract only intersected

ExtractInside.description: This parameter controls whether to extract cells that are inside or outside the region.
ExtractInside.label: Extraction Side

ImplicitFunction.description: This property sets the region used to extract cells.
ImplicitFunction.label: Intersect With

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Slice filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/ExtractCellsByType.short: Extract cells based on their type.
filters/ExtractCellsByType.description: This filter extracts cells of the selected types. If the data set does not contain cells of the chosen types, the output is empty.
filters/ExtractCellsByType.selection: Extract cells based on their type.

CellTypes.description: Select the cell types to extract.
CellTypes.label: Cell Types

Input.description: This property specifies the input of the filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/ExtractComponent.long: This filter extracts a component of a multi-component attribute array.

Component.description: This property indicates the component of the array to be extracted.
Component.label: Component

Input.description: This property specifies the input of the Extract Component filter.
Input.label: Input

OutputArrayName.description: This property indicates the name of the output scalar array.
OutputArrayName.label: Output Array Name

SelectInputArray.description: This property indicates the name of the array to be extracted.
SelectInputArray.label: Input Array

filters/ExtractEdges.long: Extract edges of 2D and 3D cells as lines.
filters/ExtractEdges.description: The Extract Edges filter produces a wireframe version of the input dataset by extracting all the edges of the dataset's cells as lines. This filter operates on any type of data set and produces polygonal output.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Extract Edges filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/ExtractEnclosedPoints.short: Extract points inside a closed points surface
filters/ExtractEnclosedPoints.long: Extract points inside a closed polygonal surface
filters/ExtractEnclosedPoints.description: Evaluates all points in the input dataset to determine whether they are contained within an enclosing surface, defined by the **Surface**. The filter assumes that the surface is closed and manifold. To force a check to ensure these preconditions are met set the **CheckSurface** property.
filters/ExtractEnclosedPoints.selection: Extract points inside a closed points surface

CheckSurface.description: Specify whether to check the surface for closure. If on, then the algorithm first checks to see if the surface is closed and manifold.
CheckSurface.label: Check Surface

GenerateOutliers.description: If checked, then a second output will be created that contains the outlier points.
GenerateOutliers.label: Generate Outliers

GenerateVertices.description: If checked, then the outputs will contain a poly-vertex cell. This takes a lot more memory, however certain filters many requires cells to be present to function properly.
GenerateVertices.label: Generate Vertices

Input.description: This property specifies the input to extract points from.
Input.label: Input

Surface.description: This property specifies the closed and manifold surface.
Surface.label: Surface

Tolerance.description: Specify the tolerance on the intersection. The tolerance is expressed as a fraction of the diagonal of the bounding box of the enclosing surface.
Tolerance.label: Tolerance

filters/GenericGeometryFilter.short: Extract geometry from a higher-order dataset
filters/GenericGeometryFilter.long: Extract geometry from a higher-order dataset
filters/GenericGeometryFilter.description: Extract geometry from a higher-order dataset.
filters/GenericGeometryFilter.selection: Extract geometry from a higher-order dataset

Input.description: Set the input to the Generic Geometry Filter.
Input.label: Input

PassThroughCellIds.description: Select whether to forward original ids.
PassThroughCellIds.label: Pass Through Cell Ids

filters/ExtractGhostCells.short: Extract ghost cells so they can be visualized.
filters/ExtractGhostCells.description: This filter extracts the ghost cells from the input and displays them so one can inspect them visually.
filters/ExtractGhostCells.selection: Extract ghost cells so they can be visualized.

ArrayName.description: Name of the ghost cell array in the output. It must be different to `vtkGhostType` in order for the cells to be displayed.
ArrayName.label: Array Name

filters/ExtractLocation.short: Sample or extracy cells at a point.
filters/ExtractLocation.long: Sample or extract cells at a point.
filters/ExtractLocation.description: This filter allows you to specify a location and then either interpolate the data attributes from the input dataset at that location or extract the cell(s) at the location.
filters/ExtractLocation.selection: Sample or extracy cells at a point.

Input.description: Set the input dataset producer
Input.label: Input

Location.description: Select the location of interest in 3D space.
Location.label: Location

Mode.description: Select whether to interpolate (probe) data attributes at the specified location, or to extract cell(s) containing the specified location.
Mode.label: Mode

filters/ExtractParticlesOverTime.short: Extract particles that pass through a volume over time.
filters/ExtractParticlesOverTime.description: This filter extracts input particles passing through a volume by iterating over time. The filter has two inputs: Particles and Volume. The Particles input should contain points evolving over time and the Volume input is expected to be a volumetric dataset. The output is a subset of the particles from the input, still temporal.
filters/ExtractParticlesOverTime.selection: Extract particles that pass through a volume over time.

IdChannelArray.description: Specify the name of a scalar array which will be used to fetch the index of each point. This is necessary only if the particles change position (Id order) on each time step. The Id can be used to identify particles at each step and hence track them properly. If this array is set to "Global or Local IDs", the global point ids are used if they exist. Otherwise, the point indices are used.
IdChannelArray.label: Id Channel Array

Particles.description: The moving particles. This input should be temporal vtkDataSet and should contain points evolving over time.
Particles.label: Particles

Volume.description: The volumetric data to detect if particles pass through. This dataset should contain volumetric cells like hexahedrons or tetrahedrons.
Volume.label: Volume

filters/DataSetRegionSurfaceFilter.long: Extract a 2D boundary surface using neighbor relations to eliminate internal faces.
filters/DataSetRegionSurfaceFilter.description: The Extract Surface filter extracts the polygons forming the outer surface of the input dataset. This filter operates on any type of data and produces polygonal data as output.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Extract Surface filter.
Input.label: Input

InterfaceIDsName.description: This the name of the input and output interface id field data array
InterfaceIDsName.label: Interface I Ds Name

MaterialIDsName.description: This the name of the input and output material id field data array
MaterialIDsName.label: Material I Ds Name

MaterialPIDsName.description: This the name of the output material ancestry id field data array
MaterialPIDsName.label: Material PI Ds Name

MaterialPropertiesName.description: This the name of the input material property field data array
MaterialPropertiesName.label: Material Properties Name

NonlinearSubdivisionLevel.description: If the input is an unstructured grid with nonlinear faces, this parameter determines how many times the face is subdivided into linear faces. If 0, the output is the equivalent of its linear counterpart (and the midpoints determining the nonlinear interpolation are discarded). If 1, the nonlinear face is triangulated based on the midpoints. If greater than 1, the triangulated pieces are recursively subdivided to reach the desired subdivision. Setting the value to greater than 1 may cause some point data to not be passed even if no quadratic faces exist. This option has no effect if the input is not an unstructured grid.
NonlinearSubdivisionLevel.label: Nonlinear Subdivision Level

PieceInvariant.description: If the value of this property is set to 1, internal surfaces along process boundaries will be removed. NOTE: Enabling this option might cause multiple executions of the data source because more information is needed to remove internal surfaces.
PieceInvariant.label: Piece Invariant

RegionArrayName.description: This property specifies the name of the material array for generating parts.
RegionArrayName.label: Region Array Name

SingleSided.description: If the value of this property is set to 1 (the default), surfaces along the boundary are 1 layer thick. Otherwise there is a surface for the material on each side.
SingleSided.label: Single Sided

filters/ExtractSelection.description: This filter extracts a set of cells/points given a selection. The selection can be obtained from a rubber-band selection (either cell, visible or in a frustum) or threshold selection and passed to the filter or specified by providing an ID list.

HyperTreeGridToUnstructuredGrid.description: Output an unstructured grid instead of a hyper tree grid (for input hyper tree grids). Should not be changed after first execution.
HyperTreeGridToUnstructuredGrid.label: Hyper Tree Grid To Unstructured Grid

Input.description: This property specifies the input from which the selection is extracted.
Input.label: Input

PreserveTopology.description: If this property is set to 1 the output preserves the topology of its input and adds an insidedness array to mark which cells are inside or out. If 0 then the output is an unstructured grid which contains only the subset of cells that are inside.
PreserveTopology.label: Preserve Topology

Selection.description: The input that provides the selection object.
Selection.label: Selection

filters/PVExtractSelection.description: This filter extracts a given set of cells or points given a selection. The selection can be obtained from a rubber-band selection (either point, cell, visible or in a frustum) and passed to the filter or specified by providing an ID list. This is an internal filter, use "ExtractSelection" instead.
filters/PVExtractSelection.selection: This filter extracts a given set of cells or points given a selection. The selection can be obtained from a rubber-band selection (either point, cell, visible or in a frustum) and passed to the filter or specified by providing an ID list. This is an internal filter, use "ExtractSelection" instead.

HyperTreeGridToUnstructuredGrid.description: Output an unstructured grid instead of a hyper tree grid for input hyper tree grids.
HyperTreeGridToUnstructuredGrid.label: Hyper Tree Grid To Unstructured Grid

Input.description: The input from which the selection is extracted.
Input.label: Input

Selection.description: The input that provides the selection object.
Selection.label: Selection

filters/ExtractGrid.long: Extract a subgrid from a structured grid with the option of setting subsample strides.
filters/ExtractGrid.description: The Extract Grid filter returns a subgrid of a structured input data set (uniform rectilinear, curvilinear, or nonuniform rectilinear). The output data set type of this filter is the same as the input type.

IncludeBoundary.description: If the value of this property is 1, then if the sample rate in any dimension is greater than 1, the boundary indices of the input dataset will be passed to the output even if the boundary extent is not an even multiple of the sample rate in a given dimension.
IncludeBoundary.label: Include Boundary

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Extract Grid filter.
Input.label: Input

SampleRateI.description: This property indicates the sampling rate in the I dimension. A value greater than 1 results in subsampling; every nth index will be included in the output.
SampleRateI.label: Sample Rate I

SampleRateJ.description: This property indicates the sampling rate in the J dimension. A value greater than 1 results in subsampling; every nth index will be included in the output.
SampleRateJ.label: Sample Rate J

SampleRateK.description: This property indicates the sampling rate in the K dimension. A value greater than 1 results in subsampling; every nth index will be included in the output.
SampleRateK.label: Sample Rate K

VOI.description: This property specifies the minimum and maximum point indices along each of the I, J, and K axes; these values indicate the volume of interest (VOI). The output will have the (I,J,K) extent specified here.
VOI.label: VOI

filters/ExtractSubsetWithSeed.long: Extract a subset from a structured-grid starting with a seed point.
filters/ExtractSubsetWithSeed.description: Extract a subset (line or plane) from a structured-grid starting with a seed point. The filter supports cases where the structured grid is split up into multiple blocks (across multiple ranks). It also handles cases were the ijk origin for each the blocks is not aligned.
filters/ExtractSubsetWithSeed.selection: Extract a subset from a structured-grid starting with a seed point.

Direction.description: Specify the direction in which to extract the slice starting with the **Seed**.
Direction.label: Direction

Seed.description: Specify the seed point in x-y-z coordinates to initiate in the slice extraction.
Seed.label: Seed

filters/DataSetSurfaceFilter.long: Extract a 2D boundary surface using neighbor relations to eliminate internal faces.
filters/DataSetSurfaceFilter.description: The Extract Surface filter extracts the polygons forming the outer surface of the input dataset. This filter operates on any type of data and produces polygonal data as output.

FastMode.description: When enabled, the filter may use approxiamte algorithm for extracting the exterior surface at the risk not being highly accurate. This may miss interior faces, for example, for structured data with blanking for better speed.
FastMode.label: Fast Mode

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Extract Surface filter.
Input.label: Input

NonlinearSubdivisionLevel.description: If the input is an unstructured grid with nonlinear faces, this parameter determines how many times the face is subdivided into linear faces. If 0, the output is the equivalent of its linear counterpart (and the midpoints determining the nonlinear interpolation are discarded). If 1, the nonlinear face is triangulated based on the midpoints. If greater than 1, the triangulated pieces are recursively subdivided to reach the desired subdivision. Setting the value to greater than 1 may cause some point data to not be passed even if no quadratic faces exist. This option has no effect if the input is not an unstructured grid.
NonlinearSubdivisionLevel.label: Nonlinear Subdivision Level

PieceInvariant.description: If the value of this property is set to 1, internal surfaces along process boundaries will be removed. NOTE: Enabling this option might cause multiple executions of the data source because more information is needed to remove internal surfaces.
PieceInvariant.label: Piece Invariant

RemoveGhostInterfaces.description: Set whether Ghost interfaces will be removed. When you are rendering you want to remove ghost interfaces. There are certain algorithms though that need the ghost interfaces.
RemoveGhostInterfaces.label: Remove Ghost Interfaces

filters/ExtractTimeSteps.description: This filter extracts specified time steps from its input.

ApproximationMode.description: If the scene's time does not match the time in any of the timesteps selected (likely because something else in the scene has time steps at different times) this setting controls which timestep should be returned by the filter. The options are the previous time step, the nearest time step and the next time step.
ApproximationMode.label: Approximation Mode

SelectionMode.description: Extract time steps supports two ways to select the time steps to be extracted: - **Select Time Steps**: Specify time steps to be extracted by their index - **Select Time Range**: Specify the start and end time steps of a range by their index and optionally specify a stride to optionally take every nth timestep in the range.
SelectionMode.label: Selection Mode

TimeStepIndices.description: This property specifies the indices of the time steps to extract.
TimeStepIndices.label: Time Step Indices

TimeStepInterval.description: Select the stride to use when extracting the range of time steps (the n in every nth timestep).
TimeStepInterval.label: Time Step Interval

TimeStepRange.description: Select the beginning and end indices of the range of timesteps to extract.
TimeStepRange.label: Time Step Range

sources/FDSReader.short: Reads .smv files outputed from the FDS code.
sources/FDSReader.description: A reader relying on `.smv` files to read outputs from the Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS) code.
sources/FDSReader.selection: Reads .smv files outputed from the FDS code.

AssemblySelectors.description: Specify the selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to extract from the input dataset.
AssemblySelectors.label: Assembly Selectors

AssemblyTag.description: This is simply an int that changes whenever a new assembly is built by the reader. This can be used to determine if the assembly should be fetched from the reader whenever the reader is updated.
AssemblyTag.label: Assembly Tag

FileName.description: This property specifies the file name for the VTKFDS reader.
FileName.label: File Name

filters/FFTSelectionOverTime.short: Extracts selection over time and plots the FFT
filters/FFTSelectionOverTime.long: Extracts selection over time and plots the FFT
filters/FFTSelectionOverTime.description: Extracts the data of a selection (e.g. points or cells) over time, takes the FFT of them, and plots them.
filters/FFTSelectionOverTime.selection: Extracts selection over time and plots the FFT

Input.description: The input from which the selection is extracted.
Input.label: Input

Selection.description: The input that provides the selection object.
Selection.label: Selection

sources/FlashParticlesReader.short: Reads AMR particles from FLASH dataset
sources/FlashParticlesReader.long: Reads AMR particles from FLASH dataset
sources/FlashParticlesReader.description: The Flash particles reader loads particle simulation data stored in Flash format. The output of this reader is a MultiBlock dataset where each block is vtkPolyData that holds the particles and corresponding particle data.
sources/FlashParticlesReader.selection: Reads AMR particles from FLASH dataset

FileNames.description: The list of files to be read by the reader.
FileNames.label: File Names

FilterLocation.description: Turns on filtering of particles by location
FilterLocation.label: Filter Location

Frequency.description: This property sets the frequency interval for loading particles.
Frequency.label: Frequency

MaxLocation.description: This property sets the minimum 3-D coordinate location by which the particles will be filtered out.
MaxLocation.label: Max Location

MinLocation.description: This property sets the minimum 3-D coordinate location by which the particles will be filtered out.
MinLocation.label: Min Location

ParticleArrayStatus.description: This property lists which particle arrays to read.
ParticleArrayStatus.label: Particle Arrays

sources/FacetReader.short: Read a dataset in Facet format.
sources/FacetReader.long: Reads ASCII files stored in Facet format.
sources/FacetReader.description: The Facet Reader reads files in Facet format: a simple ASCII file format listing point coordinates and connectivity between these points. The default file extension is .facet. The output of the Facet Reader is polygonal.
sources/FacetReader.selection: Read a dataset in Facet format.

FileName.description: This property specifies the file name for the Facet reader.
FileName.label: File Name

sources/FastUniformGrid.short: Create a 3D uniform grid with scalar and vector arrays.
sources/FastUniformGrid.long: Create a uniform grid in 3 dimensions with scalar and vector data arrays, consuming minimal computational resources.
sources/FastUniformGrid.description: The Fast Uniform Grid source can be used to create a uniform grid with scalar values derived from relatively light computations. The active scalar array is named "X", and is set to the X coordinate for each pixel. There are two additional point data sets. The data array named "DistanceSquared" is computed as the squared distance from each pixel to the origin. The data array named "Swirl" is a vector field computed as (Y,Z,X) at each pixel.
sources/FastUniformGrid.selection: Create a 3D uniform grid with scalar and vector arrays.

DesiredBytesPerPiece.description: The desired bytes per piece when the volume is split for SMP execution. When SMP is enabled, this is used to subdivide the volume into pieces. Smaller pieces allow for better dynamic load balancing, but increase the total overhead.
DesiredBytesPerPiece.label: Desired Bytes Per Piece

Generate DistanceSquared Scalars.description: Enable/disable DistanceSquared point data scalar array.
Generate DistanceSquared Scalars.label: Generate Distance Squared Scalars

Generate Swirl Vectors.description: Enable/disable Swirl point data vector array.
Generate Swirl Vectors.label: Generate Swirl Vectors

WholeExtent.description: The six values in the property indicate the X, Y, and Z extent of the output data. The first two numbers are the minimum and maximum X extent; the next two are the minimum and maximum Y extent; and the final two are the minimum and maximum Z extent. The numbers are inclusive, so values of -10, 10, -10, 10, =10, 10 indicate that the dimensions of the output will be 21 x 21 x 21.
WholeExtent.label: Whole Extent

filters/FeatureEdges.short: Extract edges that meet the feature criteria.
filters/FeatureEdges.long: This filter will extract edges along sharp edges of surfaces or boundaries of surfaces.
filters/FeatureEdges.description: The Feature Edges filter extracts various subsets of edges from the input data set. This filter operates on polygonal data and produces polygonal output.
filters/FeatureEdges.selection: Extract edges that meet the feature criteria.

BoundaryEdges.description: If the value of this property is set to 1, boundary edges will be extracted. Boundary edges are defined as lines cells or edges that are used by only one polygon.
BoundaryEdges.label: Boundary Edges

Coloring.description: If the value of this property is set to 1, then the extracted edges are assigned a scalar value based on the type of the edge.
Coloring.label: Coloring

FeatureAngle.description: The value of this property is used to define a feature edge. If the surface normal between two adjacent triangles is at least as large as this Feature Angle, a feature edge exists. (See the FeatureEdges property.)
FeatureAngle.label: Feature Angle

FeatureEdges.description: If the value of this property is set to 1, feature edges will be extracted. Feature edges are defined as edges that are used by two polygons whose dihedral angle is greater than the feature angle. (See the FeatureAngle property.) Toggle whether to extract feature edges.
FeatureEdges.label: Feature Edges

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Feature Edges filter.
Input.label: Input

ManifoldEdges.description: If the value of this property is set to 1, manifold edges will be extracted. Manifold edges are defined as edges that are used by exactly two polygons.
ManifoldEdges.label: Manifold Edges

NonManifoldEdges.description: If the value of this property is set to 1, non-manifold edges will be extracted. Non-manifold edges are defined as edges that are use by three or more polygons.
NonManifoldEdges.label: Non-Manifold Edges

sources/FidesJSONReader.description: Reader to read ADIOS2 files using Fides library. This method requires selecting the JSON file containing the Fides data model.

CellArrayStatus.description: This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
CellArrayStatus.label: Cell Arrays

CreateSharedPoints.description: This property allows Fides to close gaps between blocks of structured grids by utilizing shared points.
CreateSharedPoints.label: Create shared points

DataSourceIO.description: This property enables Fides to use the inline engine, where the writer and reader must share an ADIOS IO object. The address to an ADIOS::IO object must be passed using this property.
DataSourceIO.label: Data Source IO

FieldArrayStatus.description: This property lists which field arrays to read.
FieldArrayStatus.label: Field Arrays

FileName.description: This property sets the Fides JSON data model filename.
FileName.label: File Name

NextStepStatus.description: This property returns the status of the next step to be read. 0 means the step is ready to be read, 1 means it is not ready, and 2 means the end of the stream has been reached.
NextStepStatus.label: Next Step Status

PointArrayStatus.description: This property lists which point-centered arrays to read.
PointArrayStatus.label: Point Arrays

PrepareNextStep.description: This property has Fides/ADIOS prepare for reading the next time step when in streaming mode.
PrepareNextStep.label: PrepareNextStep

sources/FidesFileReader.description: Reader to read ADIOS2 files using Fides library.

CellArrayStatus.description: This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
CellArrayStatus.label: Cell Arrays

ConvertToVTK.description: This property determines whether data should be converted to VTK or stay in VTK-m format.
ConvertToVTK.label: Convert To VTK

CreateSharedPoints.description: This property allows Fides to close gaps between blocks of structured grids by utilizing shared points.
CreateSharedPoints.label: Create shared points

DataSourceIO.description: This property enables Fides to use the inline engine, where the writer and reader must share an ADIOS IO object. The address to an ADIOS::IO object must be passed using this property.
DataSourceIO.label: Data Source IO

FieldArrayStatus.description: This property lists which field arrays to read.
FieldArrayStatus.label: Field Arrays

FileName.description: This property sets the ADIOS2 bp filename for Fides to read.
FileName.label: File Name

NextStepStatus.description: This property returns the status of the next step to be read. 0 means the step is ready to be read, 1 means it is not ready, and 2 means the end of the stream has been reached.
NextStepStatus.label: Next Step Status

filters/GaussianSplatter.long: Splat points into a volume with an elliptical, Gaussian distribution.
filters/GaussianSplatter.description: vtkGaussianSplatter is a filter that injects input points into a structured points (volume) dataset. As each point is injected, it "splats" or distributes values to nearby voxels. Data is distributed using an elliptical, Gaussian distribution function. The distribution function is modified using scalar values (expands distribution) or normals (creates ellipsoidal distribution rather than spherical). Warning: results may be incorrect in parallel as points can't splat into other processor's cells.

Accumulation Mode.description: Specify the scalar accumulation mode. This mode expresses how scalar values are combined when splats are overlapped. The Max mode acts like a set union operation and is the most commonly used; the Min mode acts like a set intersection, and the sum is just weird.
Accumulation Mode.label: Splat Accumulation Mode

CapValue.description: Specify the cap value to use. (This instance variable only has effect if the ivar Capping is on.)
CapValue.label: Fill Value

Capping.description: Turn on/off the capping of the outer boundary of the volume to a specified cap value. This can be used to close surfaces (after isosurfacing) and create other effects.
Capping.label: Fill Volume Boundary

Eccentricity.description: Control the shape of elliptical splatting. Eccentricity is the ratio of the major axis (aligned along normal) to the minor (axes) aligned along other two axes. So Eccentricity gt 1 creates needles with the long axis in the direction of the normal; Eccentricity lt 1 creates pancakes perpendicular to the normal vector.
Eccentricity.label: Ellipitical Eccentricity

ExponentFactor.description: Set / get the sharpness of decay of the splats. This is the exponent constant in the Gaussian equation. Normally this is a negative value.
ExponentFactor.label: Gaussian Exponent Factor

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the filter.
Input.label: Input

ModelBounds.description: Set / get the (xmin,xmax, ymin,ymax, zmin,zmax) bounding box in which the sampling is performed. If any of the (min,max) bounds values are min >= max, then the bounds will be computed automatically from the input data. Otherwise, the user-specified bounds will be used.
ModelBounds.label: Extent to Resample

NormalWarping.description: Turn on/off the generation of elliptical splats. If normal warping is on, then the input normals affect the distribution of the splat. This boolean is used in combination with the Eccentricity ivar.
NormalWarping.label: Elliptical Splats

NullValue.description: Set the Null value for output points not receiving a contribution from the input points. (This is the initial value of the voxel samples.)
NullValue.label: Empty Cell Value

Radius.description: Set / get the radius of propagation of the splat. This value is expressed as a percentage of the length of the longest side of the sampling volume. Smaller numbers greatly reduce execution time.
Radius.label: Gaussian Splat Radius

SampleDimensions.description: Set / get the dimensions of the sampling structured point set. Higher values produce better results but are much slower.
SampleDimensions.label: Resampling Grid

ScalarWarping.description: Turn on/off the scaling of splats by scalar value.
ScalarWarping.label: Scale Splats

ScaleFactor.description: Multiply Gaussian splat distribution by this value. If ScalarWarping is on, then the Scalar value will be multiplied by the ScaleFactor times the Gaussian function.
ScaleFactor.label: Scale Factor

SelectInputScalars.description: Choose a scalar array to splat into the output cells. If ignore arrays is chosen, point density will be counted instead.

filters/PolyDataNormals.long: This filter will produce surface normals used for smooth shading. Splitting is used to avoid smoothing across feature edges.
filters/PolyDataNormals.description: This filter generates surface normals at the points of the input polygonal dataset to provide smooth shading of the dataset. The resulting dataset is also polygonal. The filter works by calculating a normal vector for each polygon in the dataset and then averaging the normals at the shared points.

ComputeCellNormals.description: This filter computes the normals at the points in the data set. In the process of doing this it computes polygon normals too. If you want these normals to be passed to the output of this filter, set the value of this property to 1.
ComputeCellNormals.label: Compute Cell Normals

Consistency.description: The value of this property controls whether consistent polygon ordering is enforced. Generally the normals for a data set should either all point inward or all point outward. If the value of this property is 1, then this filter will reorder the points of cells that whose normal vectors are oriented the opposite direction from the rest of those in the data set.
Consistency.label: Consistency

FeatureAngle.description: The value of this property defines a feature edge. If the surface normal between two adjacent triangles is at least as large as this Feature Angle, a feature edge exists. If Splitting is on, points are duplicated along these feature edges. (See the Splitting property.)
FeatureAngle.label: Feature Angle

FlipNormals.description: If the value of this property is 1, this filter will reverse the normal direction (and reorder the points accordingly) for all polygons in the data set; this changes front-facing polygons to back-facing ones, and vice versa. You might want to do this if your viewing position will be inside the data set instead of outside of it.

NonManifoldTraversal.description: Turn on/off traversal across non-manifold edges. Not traversing non-manifold edges will prevent problems where the consistency of polygonal ordering is corrupted due to topological loops.

PieceInvariant.description: Turn this option to to produce the same results regardless of the number of processors used (i.e., avoid seams along processor boundaries). Turn this off if you do want to process ghost levels and do not mind seams.
PieceInvariant.label: Piece Invariant

Splitting.description: This property controls the splitting of sharp edges. If sharp edges are split (property value = 1), then points are duplicated along these edges, and separate normals are computed for both sets of points to give crisp (rendered) surface definition.
Splitting.label: Splitting

Those input types (exception for vtkHyperTreeGrid) can be dispatched in vtkPartitionedDataSet or vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection. filters/Glyph.short: Generate glyphs that represent attributes in the input data set.
filters/Glyph.long: This filter produces a glyph at points or cell centers in an input data set. The glyphs can be oriented and scaled by point or cell attributes of the input dataset.
filters/Glyph.description: The Glyph filter generates a glyph (i.e., an arrow, cone, cube, cylinder, line, sphere, or 2D glyph) at each point or cell in the input dataset. The glyphs can be oriented and scaled by the input scalar and vector arrays. If the arrays are point-centered, glyphs are placed at points in the input dataset. If the arrays are cell-centered, glyphs are placed at the center of cells in the input dataset. A transform that applies to the glyph source can be modified to change the shape of the glyph. This filter operates on any type of data set. Its output is a polygonal dataset. To use this filter, select the **Orientation Array** to orient the glyphs and the **Scale Array** to control glyph scaling if desired - each array can be set to 'No array' if orientation or scaling is not desired. When scaling by a 3-element vector array, the **Vector Scale Mode** can be set to either 'Scale by Magnitude', which scales glyphs according to the vector magnitude, or 'Scale by Components', which treats each component as a separate scaling factor in the corresponding dimension, i.e., the first component is the scaling factor in the x-dimension, the second component scales the y-dimension, and the third component scales the z-dimension. An overall constant **Scale Factor** is applied following the scaling controlled by other properties of this filter. The **Glyph Mode** property controls which points in the input dataset are selected for glyphing since in most cases, glyphing all points in the input dataset can be both performance impeding as well as visually cluttered.

filters/GlyphWithCustomSource.short: Generate glyphs that represent attributes in the input data set.
filters/GlyphWithCustomSource.long: This filter produces a glyph at points or cell centers in an input data set. The glyphs can be oriented and scaled by point or cell attributes of the input dataset.
filters/GlyphWithCustomSource.description: The **Glyph With Custom Source** filter generates a glyph specified as the **Source** input to this filter at each point in the input dataset. The glyphs can be oriented and scaled by the input scalar and vector arrays. If the arrays are point-centered, glyphs are placed at points in the input dataset. If the arrays are cell-centered, glyphs are placed at the center of cells in the input dataset. A transform that applies to the glyph source can be modified to change the shape of the glyph. This filter operates on any type of data set. Its output is a polygonal dataset. To use this filter, select the **Orientation Array** to orient the glyphs and the **Scale Array** to control glyph scaling if desired - each array can be set to 'No array' if orientation or scaling is not desired. When scaling by a 3-element vector array, the **Vector Scale Mode** can be set to either 'Scale by Magnitude', which scales glyphs according to the vector magnitude, or 'Scale by Components', which treats each component as a separate scaling factor in the corresponding dimension, i.e., the first component is the scaling factor in the x-dimension, the second component scales the y-dimension, and the third component scales the z-dimension. An overall constant **Scale Factor** is applied following the scaling controlled by other properties of this filter. The **Glyph Mode** property controls which points in the input dataset are selected for glyphing since in most cases, glyphing all points in the input dataset can be both performance impeding as well as visually cluttered.

filters/Gradient.short: Compute the gradient for any type of dataset.
filters/Gradient.long: Estimate the gradient for each point or cell in any type of dataset.
filters/Gradient.description: The Gradient filter estimates the gradient vector at each point or cell. It operates on any type of vtkDataSet, and the output is of the same type as the input. For unstructured grids, the gradient is computed with the cell derivatives. For structured grids, the gradient is computed using central differencing, except on the boundary of the dataset where forward and backward differencing is used for the boundary elements. If the dataset is a vtkImageData, the gradient computation at the boundaries can also be done with central differencing using a duplication of the boundary values, smoothing out the result (see 'Boundary Method' property).
filters/Gradient.selection: Compute the gradient for any type of dataset.

BoundaryMethod.description: Specify how to compute the gradient on the boundaries. 'Smoothed' uses central differencing by duplicating the boundary values to compute the gradient on the boundary elements (corresponds to the old 'Gradient' filter). 'Non-Smoothed' uses forward/backward differencing with the values of a boundary element and its neighbor to compute the gradient (corresponds to the old 'Gradient Of Unstructured DataSet' filter).
BoundaryMethod.label: Boundary Method

ComputeDivergence.description: If on, the divergence of a 3-component array is computed.
ComputeDivergence.label: Compute Divergence

ComputeGradient.description: If on, the gradient of the input array is computed.
ComputeGradient.label: Compute Gradient

ComputeQCriterion.description: If on, the Q-criterion of a 3-component array is computed.
ComputeQCriterion.label: Compute Q Criterion

ComputeVorticity.description: If on, the vorticity/curl of a 3-component array is computed.
ComputeVorticity.label: Compute Vorticity

ContributingCellOption.description: Specify which dimensions of cells should be used when computing gradient quantities. Default is to use the dataset maximum cell dimension.

Dimensionality.description: Specify whether to compute the gradient in two or three dimensions. In two dimensions, the X and Y dimensions are used.

DivergenceArrayName.description: Provide a name for the output array containing the divergence vector.

ExtensiveComputation.description: Use the extensive ratio during the Hyper Tree Grid gradient computation. This property only work in UNLIMITED mode.

FasterApproximation.description: If on, the Gradient filter will provide a less accurate (but close) algorithm that performs fewer derivative calculations (and is therefore faster). The error contains some smoothing of the output data and some possible errors on the boundary. Has no effect when performing the gradient of cell data or when the input grid is not a vtkUnstructuredGrid.
FasterApproximation.label: Faster Approximation

HTGMode.description: Specify how to compute the gradient on a Hypertree Grid. 'Unlimited' handles the resolution change by virtually subdividing coarser cells and eventually applyging a ratio. 'Unstructured' operate like the AMR like if it was an unstructured mesh, which may give a higher weight to coarser cells.
HTGMode.label: HTG Mode

Input.label: Input

QCriterionArrayName.label: Q Criterion Array Name

filters/KMeans.short: Compute a statistical model of a dataset and/or assess the dataset with a statistical model.
filters/KMeans.long: Compute a statistical model of a dataset and/or assess the dataset with a statistical model.
filters/KMeans.description:
This filter either computes a statistical model of a dataset or takes such a model as its second input. Then, the model (however it is obtained) may optionally be used to assess the input dataset.

This filter iteratively computes the center of k clusters in a space whose coordinates are specified by the arrays you select. The clusters are chosen as local minima of the sum of square Euclidean distances from each point to its nearest cluster center. The model is then a set of cluster centers. Data is assessed by assigning a cluster center and distance to the cluster to each point in the input data set.

Task.description:
Specify the task to be performed: modeling and/or assessment.
  1. "Detailed model of input data," creates a set of output tables containing a calculated statistical model of the entire input dataset;
  2. "Model a subset of the data," creates an output table (or tables) summarizing a randomly-chosen subset of the input dataset;
  3. "Assess the data with a model," adds attributes to the first input dataset using a model provided on the second input port; and
  4. "Model and assess the same data," is really just operations 2 and 3 above applied to the same input dataset. The model is first trained using a fraction of the input data and then the entire dataset is assessed using that model.
When the task includes creating a model (i.e., tasks 2, and 4), you may adjust the fraction of the input dataset used for training. You should avoid using a large fraction of the input data for training as you will then not be able to detect overfitting. The Training fraction setting will be ignored for tasks 1 and 3.

StaticSeeds.label: Static Seeds

TerminalSpeed.description: This property specifies the terminal speed, below which particle advection/integration is terminated.
TerminalSpeed.label: Terminal Speed

TerminationTime.description: Setting TerminationTime to a positive value will cause particles to terminate when the time is reached. The units of time should be consistent with the primary time variable.
TerminationTime.label: Termination Time

filters/LegacyStreakLine.short: Trace Streak lines through time in a vector field.
filters/LegacyStreakLine.long: Trace Streak lines through time in a vector field.
filters/LegacyStreakLine.description: The Particle Trace filter generates pathlines in a vector field from a collection of seed points. The vector field used is selected from the Vectors menu, so the input data set is required to have point-centered vectors. The Seed portion of the interface allows you to select whether the seed points for this integration lie in a point cloud or along a line. Depending on which is selected, the appropriate 3D widget (point or line widget) is displayed along with traditional user interface controls for positioning the point cloud or line within the data set. Instructions for using the 3D widgets and the corresponding manual controls can be found in section 7.4. This filter operates on any type of data set, provided it has point-centered vectors. The output is polygonal data containing polylines.
filters/LegacyStreakLine.selection: Trace Streak lines through time in a vector field.

ComputeVorticity.description: Compute vorticity and angular rotation of particles as they progress
ComputeVorticity.label: Compute Vorticity

DisableResetCache.description: Prevents cache from getting reset so that new computation always start from previous results.
DisableResetCache.label: Disable Reset Cache

ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps.description: When animating particles, it is nice to inject new ones every Nth step to produce a continuous flow. Setting ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps to a non zero value will cause the particle source to reinject particles every Nth step even if it is otherwise unchanged. Note that if the particle source is also animated, this flag will be redundant as the particles will be reinjected whenever the source changes anyway.
ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps.label: Force Reinjection Every N Steps

Input.description: Specify which is the Input of the StreamTracer filter.

InterpolatorType.description: This property determines which interpolator to use for evaluating the velocity vector field. The first is faster though the second is more robust in locating cells during streamline integration.
InterpolatorType.label: Interpolator Type

MeshOverTime.description: The input mesh can either be 1) different over time, or 2) static over time, or 3) a linear transformation of the first time step over time, or 4) have the same topology over time. If a value other than Different are used, then performance can be improved significantly because certain data structures, such as locators or cell links are not rebuilt for each timestep.
MeshOverTime.label: Mesh Over Time

SelectInputVectors.description: Specify which vector array should be used for the integration through that filter.
SelectInputVectors.label: Select Input Vectors

Source.description: Specify the seed dataset. Typically, from where the vector field integration should begin. Usually a point/radius or a line with a given resolution.
Source.label: Seed Source

StaticSeeds.description: If the input seeds are not changing, then this can be set to 1 to avoid having to do a repeated grid search that would return the exact same result.

filters/LinearCellExtrusionFilter.long: This filter creates a swept surface defined by translating the input along a vector.
filters/LinearCellExtrusionFilter.description: The Linear Extrusion filter creates a swept surface by translating the input dataset along the cell normals or a specified vector. This filter is intended to operate on polygonal data and produces 3D unstructured grid output.

filters/LinearExtrusionFilter.long: This filter creates a swept surface defined by translating the input along a vector.
filters/LinearExtrusionFilter.description: The Linear Extrusion filter creates a swept surface by translating the input dataset along a specified vector. This filter is intended to operate on 2D polygonal data. This filter operates on polygonal data and produces polygonal data output.

Capping.description: The value of this property indicates whether to cap the ends of the swept surface. Capping works by placing a copy of the input dataset on either end of the swept surface, so it behaves properly if the input is a 2D surface composed of filled polygons. If the input dataset is a closed solid (e.g., a sphere), then if capping is on (i.e., this property is set to 1), two copies of the data set will be displayed on output (the second translated from the first one along the specified vector). If instead capping is off (i.e., this property is set to 0), then an input closed solid will produce no output.
Capping.label: Capping

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Linear Extrusion filter.
Input.label: Input

PieceInvariant.description: The value of this property determines whether the output will be the same regardless of the number of processors used to compute the result. The difference is whether there are internal polygonal faces on the processor boundaries. A value of 1 will keep the results the same; a value of 0 will allow internal faces on processor boundaries.

ScaleFactor.description: The value of this property determines the distance along the vector the dataset will be translated. (A scale factor of 0.5 will move the dataset half the length of the vector, and a scale factor of 2 will move it twice the vector's length.)

It is named for Charles Loop, the person who devised this subdivision scheme. This filter only operates on triangles, so a data set that contains other types of polygons should be passed through the Triangulate filter before applying this filter to it. This filter only operates on polygonal data (specifically triangle meshes), and it produces polygonal output.

sources/ImageMandelbrotSource.long: Representation (unsigned char) of the Mandlebrot set in up to 3 dimensions
sources/ImageMandelbrotSource.description: The Mandelbrot source can be used to add a uniform rectilinear grid with scalar values derived from the Mandelbrot set to the 3D scene. The equation used is z = z^2 + C (where z and C are complex, and C is a constant). The scalar values in the grid are the number of iterations of the equation it takes for the magnitude of the value to become greater than 2. In the equation, the initial value of z is 0. By default, the real component of C is mapped onto the X axis; the imaginary component of C is mapped onto the Y axis; and the imaginary component of the initial value is mapped onto the Z axis. If a two-dimensional extent is specified, the resulting image will be displayed. If a three-dimensional extent is used, then the bounding box of the volume will be displayed. The output of the Mandelbrot source is image (uniform rectilinear) data.

MaximumNumberOfIterations.description: The value of this property specifies the limit on computational iterations (i.e., the maximum number of iterations to perform to determine if the value will go above 2). Values less than 2.0 after the specified number of iterations are considered in the fractal set.
MaximumNumberOfIterations.label: Maximum Number of Iterations

OriginCX.description: The four values of this property indicate (in order) the components of C (real and imaginary) and the components of the initial value, X (real and imaginary).
OriginCX.label: Origin CX

ProjectionAxes.description: The three values in this property allow you to specify the projection from the 4D space used by the Mandelbrot set to the axes of the 3D volume. By default, the real component of C (represented by 0) is mapped to the X axis; the imaginary component of C (represented by 1) is mapped to the Y axis; and the real component of X, the initial value (represented by 2) is mapped to the Z axis. The imaginary component of X is represented by 3. All values entered must be between 0 and 3, inclusive.
ProjectionAxes.label: Projection Axes

SizeCX.description: The four values of this property indicate the length of the output in each of the four dimensions (the real and imaginary components of C and the real and imaginary components of X). The three dimensions specified in the Projection Axes property will determine which of these values specify the length of the axes in the output.
SizeCX.label: Size CX

SubsampleRate.description: This property specifies the rate at which to subsample the volume. The extent of the dataset in each dimension will be divided by this value.
SubsampleRate.label: Subsample Rate

WholeExtent.description: The six values in the property indicate the X, Y, and Z extent of the output data. The first two numbers are the minimum and maximum X extent; the next two are the minimum and maximum Y extent; and the final two are the minimum and maximum Z extent. The numbers are inclusive, so values of 0, 250, 0, 250, 0, 0 indicate that the dimensions of the output will be 251 x 251 x 1.
WholeExtent.label: Whole Extent

filters/MaskPoints.description: The Mask Points filter reduces the number of points in the dataset. It operates on any type of dataset, but produces only points / vertices as output.

Offset.description: The value of this property indicates the starting point id in the ordered list of input points from which to start masking.

OnRatio.description: The value of this property specifies that every OnStride-th points will be retained in the output when not using Random (the skip or stride size for point ids). ProportionalMaximumNumberOfPoints.description: When this is off, the maximum number of points is taken per processor when running in parallel (total number of points = number of processors * maximum number of points). When this is on, the maximum number of points is proportionally distributed across processors depending on the number of points per processor ("total number of points" is the same as "maximum number of points" maximum number of points per processor = number of points on a processor * maximum number of points / total number of points across all processors ).
ProportionalMaximumNumberOfPoints.label: Proportionally Distribute Maximum Number Of Points

RandomMode.description: If the value of this property is set to true, then the points in the output will be randomly selected from the input in various ways set by Random Mode; otherwise this filter will subsample point ids regularly.

RandomModeType.description: Randomized Id Strides picks points with random id increments starting at Offset (the output probably isn't a statistically random sample). Random Sampling generates a statistically random sample of the input, ignoring Offset (fast - O(sample size)). Spatially Stratified Random Sampling is a variant of random sampling that splits the points into equal sized spatial strata before randomly sampling (slow - O(N log N)). The Uniform Spatial Distribution (Bound based) samples points using random poisitions inside the bounds of the data set and a point locator. The Uniform Spatial Distribution (Surface Sampling) samples points randomly via an inverse transform on surface area of each cell (3D cells are ignored). The Uniform Spatial Distribution (Volume Sampling) samples points randomly sampled via an inverse transform on volume area of each cell (2D cells are ignored).
RandomModeType.label: Random Sampling Mode

filters/MaterialInterfaceFilter.short: The Material Interface filter finds volumes in the input data containing material above a certain material fraction.
filters/MaterialInterfaceFilter.long: The Material Interface filter finds volumes in the input data containing material above a certain material fraction.
filters/MaterialInterfaceFilter.description: The Material Interface filter finds voxels inside of which a material fraction (or normalized amount of material) is higher than a given threshold. As these voxels are identified surfaces enclosing adjacent voxels above the threshold are generated. The resulting volume and its surface are what we call a fragment. The filter has the ability to compute various volumetric attributes such as fragment volume, mass, center of mass as well as volume and mass weighted averages for any of the fields present. Any field selected for such computation will be also be copied into the fragment surface's point data for visualization. The filter also has the ability to generate Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBB) for each fragment. The data generated by the filter is organized in three outputs. The "geometry" output, containing the fragment surfaces. The "statistics" output, containing a point set of the centers of mass. The "obb representation" output, containing OBB representations (poly data). All computed attributes are copied into the statistics and geometry output. The obb representation output is used for validation and debugging purposes and is turned off by default. To measure the size of craters, the filter can invert a volume fraction and clip the volume fraction with a sphere and/or a plane.

A warning is generated if no mass array is selected for an individual material fraction array. However, in that case the filter will run without issue because the statistics output can be generated using fragments' centers computed from axis aligned bounding boxes.

filters/MulticorrelativeStatistics.short: Compute a statistical model of a dataset and/or assess the dataset with a statistical model.
filters/MulticorrelativeStatistics.long: Compute a statistical model of a dataset and/or assess the dataset with a statistical model.
filters/MulticorrelativeStatistics.description:
This filter either computes a statistical model of a dataset or takes such a model as its second input. Then, the model (however it is obtained) may optionally be used to assess the input dataset.

This filter computes the covariance matrix for all the arrays you select plus the mean of each array. The model is thus a multivariate Gaussian distribution with the mean vector and variances provided. Data is assessed using this model by computing the Mahalanobis distance for each input point. This distance will always be positive.

The learned model output format is rather dense and can be confusing, so it is discussed here. The first filter output is a multiblock dataset consisting of 2 tables:

  1. Raw covariance data.
  2. Covariance matrix and its Cholesky decomposition.
The raw covariance table has 3 meaningful columns: 2 titled "Column1" and "Column2" whose entries generally refer to the N arrays you selected when preparing the filter and 1 column titled "Entries" that contains numeric values. The first row will always contain the number of observations in the statistical analysis. The next N rows contain the mean for each of the N arrays you selected. The remaining rows contain covariances of pairs of arrays.

The second table (covariance matrix and Cholesky decomposition) contains information derived from the raw covariance data of the first table. The first N rows of the first column contain the name of one array you selected for analysis. These rows are followed by a single entry labeled "Cholesky" for a total of N+1 rows. The second column, Mean contains the mean of each variable in the first N entries and the number of observations processed in the final (N+1) row.

The remaining columns (there are N, one for each array) contain 2 matrices in triangular format. The upper right triangle contains the covariance matrix (which is symmetric, so its lower triangle may be inferred). The lower left triangle contains the Cholesky decomposition of the covariance matrix (which is triangular, so its upper triangle is zero). Because the diagonal must be stored for both matrices, an additional row is required â€” hence the N+1 rows and the final entry of the column named "Column".

Task.description:
Specify the task to be performed: modeling and/or assessment.
  1. "Detailed model of input data," creates a set of output tables containing a calculated statistical model of the entire input dataset;
  2. "Model a subset of the data," creates an output table (or tables) summarizing a randomly-chosen subset of the input dataset;
  3. "Assess the data with a model," adds attributes to the first input dataset using a model provided on the second input port; and
  4. "Model and assess the same data," is really just operations 2 and 3 above applied to the same input dataset. The model is first trained using a fraction of the input data and then the entire dataset is assessed using that model.
When the task includes creating a model (i.e., tasks 2, and 4), you may adjust the fraction of the input dataset used for training. You should avoid using a large fraction of the input data for training as you will then not be able to detect overfitting. The Training fraction setting will be ignored for tasks 1 and 3.

sources/MPASReader.description: This reader reads unstructured grid MPAS data from a file. It creates a dual grid It assumes the grid is in the global domain. By default, it creates a spherical view of vertical layer 0. It assumes it is ocean data. It gives several options to change the view to multilayer (all vertical layers will have a thickness determined by the value in the slider), lat/lon projection or atmospheric (vertical layers go out away from the center of the sphere, instead of down towards the center as they do for ocean data). It doesn't handle data in the rectangular domain. This is not a parallel reader. It expects one .nc file of data. It can display cell or vertex-centered data, but not edge data. When converted to the dual grid, cell-centered data becomes vertex-centered and vice-versa. NOTES: When using this reader, it is important that you remember to do the following: 1. When changing a selected variable, remember to select it also in the drop down box to color by. It doesn't color by that variable automatically 2. When selecting multilayer sphere view, start with layer thickness around 100,000 3. When selecting multilayer lat/lon view, start with layer thickness around 10 4. Always click the -Z orientation after making a switch from lat/lon to sphere, from single to multilayer or changing thickness. 5. Be conservative on the number of changes you make before hitting Apply, since there may be bugs in this reader. Just make one change and then hit Apply. For problems, contact Christine Ahrens (cahrens@lanl.gov)

Unfortunately, it is not a self-describing format therefore the user needs to pass information about the contents of the file to the reader. Normally, this is done by setting a number of member variables. The goal of this reader is to provide a simple format that enable the writer of the PLOT3D file to describe its settings as well as group a number of files as a time series.

The default file extension for the geometry files is .xyz, and the default file extension for the solution files is .q. The output of this reader is a multiblock dataset containing curvilinear (structured grid) datasets. This is a distributed reader.

filters/ParticlePath.description: The Particle Trace filter generates pathlines in a vector field from a collection of seed points. The vector field used is selected from the Vectors menu, so the input data set is required to have point-centered vectors. The Seed portion of the interface allows you to select whether the seed points for this integration lie in a point cloud or along a line. Depending on which is selected, the appropriate 3D widget (point or line widget) is displayed along with traditional user interface controls for positioning the point cloud or line within the data set. Instructions for using the 3D widgets and the corresponding manual controls can be found in section 7.4. This filter operates on any type of data set, provided it has point-centered vectors. The output is polygonal data containing polylines. This filter is available on the Toolbar.

Setting ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps to a non zero value will cause the particle source to reinject particles every Nth step even if it is otherwise unchanged. Note that if the particle source is also animated, this flag will be redundant as the particles will be reinjected whenever the source changes anyway.

sources/ParticleReader.description: vtkParticleReader reads either a binary or a text file of particles. Each particle can have associated with it an optional scalar value. So the format is: x, y, z, scalar (all floats or doubles). The text file can consist of a comma delimited set of values. In most cases vtkParticleReader can automatically determine whether the file is text or binary. The data can be either float or double. Progress updates are provided. With respect to binary files, random access into the file to read pieces is supported.

filters/PartitionBalancer.short: Evens the number of partitions across ranks
filters/PartitionBalancer.description: Evens the number of partitions across ranks, while discarding empty partitions of the input There are two ways this filter will balance the input. If Squash is selected, empty partitions are appended to ranks having less partitions than the rank with the most partitions. If Expand is selected, then the number of partitions in the output is equal to the number of partitions if all partitions were sent to one rank. For a given rank, the indices of non empty partitions in the output map to empty partitions in every other ranks.

This filter operates on any type of data and produces a polygonal output (a polyline). One can use different sampling patterns with this filter. "Sample At Cell Boundaries" gives the most accurate plots, "Sample At Segment Centers" provides one sample per probed cell, and "Sample Uniformally" samples uniformally along the input line.

filters/PCAStatistics.short: Compute a statistical model of a dataset and/or assess the dataset with a statistical model.
filters/PCAStatistics.long: Compute a statistical model of a dataset and/or assess the dataset with a statistical model.
filters/PCAStatistics.description:
This filter either computes a statistical model of a dataset or takes such a model as its second input. Then, the model (however it is obtained) may optionally be used to assess the input dataset.

This filter performs additional analysis above and beyond the multicorrelative filter. It computes the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix from the multicorrelative filter. Data is then assessed by projecting the original tuples into a possibly lower-dimensional space.

Since the PCA filter uses the multicorrelative filter's analysis, it shares the same raw covariance table specified in the multicorrelative documentation. The second table in the multiblock dataset comprising the model output is an expanded version of the multicorrelative version.

As with the multicorrelative filter, the second model table contains the mean values, the upper-triangular portion of the symmetric covariance matrix, and the non-zero lower-triangular portion of the Cholesky decomposition of the covariance matrix. Below these entries are the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix (in the column labeled "Mean") and the eigenvectors (as row vectors) in an additional NxN matrix.
filters/PCAStatistics.selection: Compute a statistical model of a dataset and/or assess the dataset with a statistical model.

AttributeMode.description: Specify which type of field data the arrays will be drawn from.

BasisEnergy.description: The minimum energy to use when determining the dimensionality of the new space into which the assessment will project tuples.
BasisEnergy.label: Basis Energy

BasisScheme.description:
When reporting assessments, should the full eigenvector decomposition be used to project the original vector into the new space (Full basis), or should a fixed subset of the decomposition be used (Fixed-size basis), or should the projection be clipped to preserve at least some fixed "energy" (Fixed-energy basis)?

As an example, suppose the variables of interest were {A,B,C,D,E} and that the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix for these were {5,2,1.5,1,.5}. If the "Full basis" scheme is used, then all 5 components of the eigenvectors will be used to project each {A,B,C,D,E}-tuple in the original data into a new 5-components space.

If the "Fixed-size" scheme is used and the "Basis Size" property is set to 4, then only the first 4 eigenvector components will be used to project each {A,B,C,D,E}-tuple into the new space and that space will be of dimension 4, not 5.

If the "Fixed-energy basis" scheme is used and the "Basis Energy" property is set to 0.8, then only the first 3 eigenvector components will be used to project each {A,B,C,D,E}-tuple into the new space, which will be of dimension 3. The number 3 is chosen because 3 is the lowest N for which the sum of the first N eigenvalues divided by the sum of all eigenvalues is larger than the specified "Basis Energy" (i.e., (5+2+1.5)/10 = 0.85 > 0.8).
BasisScheme.label: Basis Scheme

BasisSize.description: The maximum number of eigenvector components to use when projecting into the new space.
BasisSize.label: Basis Size

Input.description: The input to the filter. Arrays from this dataset will be used for computing statistics and/or assessed by a statistical model.

ModelInput.description: A previously-calculated model with which to assess a separate dataset. This input is optional.

NormalizationScheme.description: Before the eigenvector decomposition of the covariance matrix takes place, you may normalize each (i,j) entry by sqrt( cov(i,i) * cov(j,j) ). This implies that the variance of each variable of interest should be of equal importance.
NormalizationScheme.label: Normalization Scheme

RobustPCA.description: Compute robust PCA with medians instead of means.

SelectArrays.description: Choose arrays whose entries will be used to form observations for statistical analysis.
SelectArrays.label: Variables of Interest

Task.description:
Specify the task to be performed: modeling and/or assessment.
  1. "Detailed model of input data," creates a set of output tables containing a calculated statistical model of the entire input dataset;
  2. "Model a subset of the data," creates an output table (or tables) summarizing a randomly-chosen subset of the input dataset;
  3. "Assess the data with a model," adds attributes to the first input dataset using a model provided on the second input port; and
  4. "Model and assess the same data," is really just operations 2 and 3 above applied to the same input dataset. The model is first trained using a fraction of the input data and then the entire dataset is assessed using that model.
When the task includes creating a model (i.e., tasks 2, and 4), you may adjust the fraction of the input dataset used for training. You should avoid using a large fraction of the input data for training as you will then not be able to detect overfitting. The Training fraction setting will be ignored for tasks 1 and 3.
Task.label: Task

TrainingFraction.description: Specify the fraction of values from the input dataset to be used for model fitting. The exact set of values is chosen at random from the dataset.
