GenerateCellData.description: The value of this property determines whether to generate process id for cells.
GenerateCellData.label: Generate Cell Data

GeneratePointData.description: The value of this property determines whether to generate process id for points.
GeneratePointData.label: Generate Point Data

sources/Protractor.long: This is a poly-line source that can be used to measure an angle between 3 points
sources/Protractor.description: The protractor can be used to interactively (using a 3D widget) or manually (using the entries on the user interface) specify 3 points and then determine the angle between these three. To place points on the surface of any dataset, one can use the 'p' key shortcut.

filters/QuadricClustering.long: This filter is the same filter used to generate level of detail for ParaView.  It uses a structured grid of bins and merges all points contained in each bin.
filters/QuadricClustering.description: The Quadric Clustering filter produces a reduced-resolution polygonal approximation of the input polygonal dataset. This filter is the one used by ParaView for computing LODs. It uses spatial binning to reduce the number of points in the data set; points that lie within the same spatial bin are collapsed into one representative point.

CopyCellData.description: If this property is set to 1, the cell data from the input will be copied to the output.
CopyCellData.label: Copy Cell Data

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Quadric Clustering filter.
Input.label: Input

NumberOfDivisions.description: This property specifies the number of bins along the X, Y, and Z axes of the data set.
NumberOfDivisions.label: Number of Dimensions

UseFeatureEdges.description: If this property is set to 1, feature edge quadrics will be used to maintain the boundary edges along processor divisions.
UseFeatureEdges.label: Use Feature Edges

UseFeaturePoints.description: If this property is set to 1, feature point quadrics will be used to maintain the boundary points along processor divisions.
UseFeaturePoints.label: Use Feature Points

UseInputPoints.description: If the value of this property is set to 1, the representative point for each bin is selected from one of the input points that lies in that bin; the input point that produces the least error is chosen. If the value of this property is 0, the location of the representative point is calculated to produce the least error possible for that bin, but the point will most likely not be one of the input points.
UseInputPoints.label: Use Input Points

UseInternalTriangles.description: If this property is set to 1, triangles completely contained in a spatial bin will be included in the computation of the bin's quadrics. When this property is set to 0, the filters operates faster, but the resulting surface may not be as well-behaved.
UseInternalTriangles.label: Use Internal Triangles

sources/RTXMLPolyDataReader.selection: Read XML polydata through the native real-time reader; file availability and update semantics require explicit review.

FileName.description: Set the file name for the real-time VTK polygonal dataset reader.
FileName.label: File Name

Location.description: Set the data directory containing real time data files.
Location.label: Location

filters/RandomAttributeGenerator.long: This filter creates a new random attribute                       array and sets it as the default array.
filters/RandomAttributeGenerator.description: The Random Attributes filter creates random attributes including scalars and vectors. These attributes can be generated as point data or cell data. The generation of each component is normalized between a user-specified minimum and maximum value. This filter provides that capability to specify the data type of the attributes and the range for each of the components. Note that in the case of an input HTG, only cell random attribute generation is available.

AttributesConstantPerBlock.description: Indicate that the generated attributes are constant within a block. This can be used to highlight blocks in a composite dataset.
AttributesConstantPerBlock.label: Attributes Constant Per Block

ComponentRange.description: Set the range values (minimum and maximum) for each component. This applies to all data that is generated.
ComponentRange.label: Component Range

DataType.description: Specify the type of array to create (all components of this array are of this type). This holds true for all arrays that are created.
DataType.label: Data Type

GenerateCellScalars.description: Indicate that point scalars are to be generated.
GenerateCellScalars.label: Generate Cell Scalars

GenerateCellVectors.description: Indicate that point vectors are to be generated.
GenerateCellVectors.label: Generate Cell Vectors

GeneratePointScalars.description: Indicate that point scalars are to be generated.
GeneratePointScalars.label: Generate Point Scalars

GeneratePointVectors.description: Indicate that point vectors are to be generated.
GeneratePointVectors.label: Generate Point Vectors

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Random Scalars filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/BrownianPoints.short: Create a new random vector array.
filters/BrownianPoints.long: This filter creates a new 3-component point data array and sets it as the default vector array. It uses a random number generator to create values.
filters/BrownianPoints.description: The Random Vectors filter generates a point-centered array of random vectors. It uses a random number generator to determine the components of the vectors. This filter operates on any type of dataset, and the output dataset will be of the same type as the input.
filters/BrownianPoints.selection: Create a new random vector array.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Random Vectors filter.
Input.label: Input

MaximumSpeed.description: This property specifies the maximum length of the random point vectors generated.
MaximumSpeed.label: Maximum Speed

MinimumSpeed.description: This property specifies the minimum length of the random point vectors generated.
MinimumSpeed.label: Minimum Speed

filters/RectilinearGridToPointSet.short: Converts a rectilinear grid to an       equivalent structured grid
filters/RectilinearGridToPointSet.description: The Rectilinear Grid to Point Set filter takes a rectilinear grid object and produces an equivalent Structured Grid, which is a type of point set. This brings the data to a broader category of data storage but only adds a small amount of overhead. This filter can be helpful in applying filters that expect or manipulate point coordinates.
filters/RectilinearGridToPointSet.selection: Converts a rectilinear grid to an       equivalent structured grid

filters/RectilinearGridConnectivity.short: Parallel fragments extraction and attributes integration on rectilinear grids.
filters/RectilinearGridConnectivity.long: Parallel fragments extraction and attributes integration on rectilinear grids.
filters/RectilinearGridConnectivity.description: Extracts material fragments from multiblock vtkRectilinearGrid datasets based on the selected volume fraction array(s) and a fraction isovalue and integrates the associated attributes.
filters/RectilinearGridConnectivity.selection: Parallel fragments extraction and attributes integration on rectilinear grids.

AddDoubleVolumeArrayName.description: This property specifies the name(s) of the volume fraction array(s) for generating parts.
AddDoubleVolumeArrayName.label: Double Volume Arrays

AddFloatVolumeArrayName.description: This property specifies the name(s) of the volume fraction array(s) for generating parts.
AddFloatVolumeArrayName.label: Float Volume Arrays

AddUnsignedCharVolumeArrayName.description: This property specifies the name(s) of the volume fraction array(s) for generating parts.
AddUnsignedCharVolumeArrayName.label: Unsigned Character Volume Arrays

Input.description: This property specifies the input of the filter.
Input.label: Input

VolumeFractionSurfaceValue.description: The value of this property is the volume fraction value for the surface.
VolumeFractionSurfaceValue.label: Volume Fraction Value

filters/RectilinearGridGeometryFilter.short: Extracts geometry for a rectilinear grid.
filters/RectilinearGridGeometryFilter.long: Extracts geometry for a rectilinear grid.  Output is a polydata dataset.
filters/RectilinearGridGeometryFilter.description: RectilinearGridGeometryFilter is a filter that extracts geometry from a rectilinear grid. By specifying appropriate i-j-k indices, it is possible to extract a point, a curve, a surface, or a "volume". The volume is actually a (n x m x o) region of points. The extent specification is zero-offset. That is, the first k-plane in a 50x50x50 rectilinear grid is given by (0,49, 0,49, 0,0).
filters/RectilinearGridGeometryFilter.selection: Extracts geometry for a rectilinear grid.

Input.description: Set the input to the Rectilinear Grid Geometry filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/RedistributeDataSet.long: Redistribute dataset into requested number of partitions.
filters/RedistributeDataSet.description: Redistribute data for load balancing. The filter either computes the bounding boxes, or uses a provided collection of bounding boxes, for distributing the data. Cells along partition boundaries can be uniquely assigned to a partition, duplicated among partitions, or split among the partitions. The output is an unstructured grid.
filters/RedistributeDataSet.selection: Redistribute dataset into requested number of partitions.

BoundaryMode.description: This property determines how cells that lie on processor boundaries are handled. The "Assign to one region" option assigns each boundary cell to exactly one process, which is useful for isosurfacing. Selecting "Assign to all regions" causes the cells on the boundaries to be copied to each process that shares that boundary. The "Split cells" option breaks cells across process boundary lines so that pieces of the cell lie in different processes. This option is useful for volume rendering.
BoundaryMode.label: Boundary Mode

EnableDebugging.description: Retains some helper arrays created for generating global cell Ids and ghost cells that are useful for debugging.
EnableDebugging.label: Enable Debugging

GenerateGlobalCellIds.description: Generate global Ids for all cells across partitions.
GenerateGlobalCellIds.label: Generate Global Cell Ids

LoadBalanceAcrossAllBlocks.description: When checked, for datasets with multiple blocks, the filter will try to load balance across all blocks otherwise each block is separately load balanced.
LoadBalanceAcrossAllBlocks.label: Load Balance Across All Blocks

NumberOfPartitions.description: Specify the number of partitions to split the dataset into. Set to 0 to indicate that the partitions should match the number of ranks. The value provided is a hint and the actual number of partitions will be equal to the power of 2 greater than or equal to the chosen value.
NumberOfPartitions.label: Number Of Partitions

PreservePartitionsInOutput.description: When unchecked, ranks with more than one partition will merge the partitions into a single vtkUnstructuredGrid. When checked, the partitions are preserved and the output is a vtkPartitionedDataSet.
PreservePartitionsInOutput.label: Preserve Partitions In Output

filters/ReductionFilter.selection: Reduce native datasets using the selected reduction pipeline; no universal numerical reduction is inferred.

GenerateProcessIds.description: If true, the filter will generate vtkOriginalProcessIds arrays indicating the process id on which the cell/point was generated.
GenerateProcessIds.label: Generate Process Ids

Input.description: Set the input to the Reduction filter.
Input.label: Input

PassThrough.description: If set to a non-negative value, then produce results using only the node Id specified.
PassThrough.label: Pass Through

PostGatherHelperName.description: Set the algorithm that takes multiple inputs and produces a single reduced output.
PostGatherHelperName.label: Post Gather Helper Name

PreGatherHelperName.description: Set the algorithm that runs on each node in parallel.
PreGatherHelperName.label: Pre Gather Helper Name

filters/ReflectionFilter.short: Reflect input over an axis aligned plane.
filters/ReflectionFilter.long: This filter takes the union of the input and its reflection over an axis-aligned plane.
filters/ReflectionFilter.description: The Reflect filter reflects the input dataset across the specified plane. This filter operates on any type of data set and produces an unstructured grid output.
filters/ReflectionFilter.selection: Reflect input over an axis aligned plane.

Center.description: If the value of the Plane property is X, Y, or Z, then the value of this property specifies the center of the reflection plane.
Center.label: Center

CopyInput.description: If this property is set to 1, the output will contain the union of the input dataset and its reflection. Otherwise the output will contain only the reflection of the input data.
CopyInput.label: Copy Input

FlipAllInputArrays.description: If off, only Vectors, Normals and Tensors will be flipped. If on, all 3-component data arrays ( considered as 3D vectors), 6-component data arrays (considered as symmetric tensors), 9-component data arrays (considered as tensors ) of signed type will be flipped. All other arrays won't be flipped and will only be copied.
FlipAllInputArrays.label: Flip All Input Arrays

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Reflect filter.
Input.label: Input

Plane.description: The value of this property determines which plane to reflect across. If the value is X, Y, or Z, the value of the Center property determines where the plane is placed along the specified axis. The other six options (X Min, X Max, etc.) place the reflection plane at the specified face of the bounding box of the input dataset.
Plane.label: Plane

sources/MultiServerProxy.short: This proxy allow the user to automatically embed inside a built-in session data objects that belong to other servers
sources/MultiServerProxy.long: This proxy allow the user to automatically embed inside a built-in session data objects that belong to other servers
sources/MultiServerProxy.selection: This proxy allow the user to automatically embed inside a built-in session data objects that belong to other servers

filters/RemoveGhostInformation.description: Removes ghost cells, point data and cell data ghost arrays. In the case of HyperTree Grid input, this filter removes the cell data ghost array and masks the ghost cells.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the remove ghost information filter. This filter operates on unstructured grids and polydata since it removes the ghost cells. It also supports HTGs, in which case it simply masks ghost cells.
Input.label: Input

filters/RenameArrays.description: This forwards the data to the output and allow to modify array names in place.

CellArrayNames.description: This property associates new names to the input cell array names
CellArrayNames.label: Cell Arrays

EdgeArrayNames.description: This property associates new names to the input edge array names
EdgeArrayNames.label: Edge Arrays

FieldArrayNames.description: This property associates new names to the input field array names
FieldArrayNames.label: Field Arrays

PointArrayNames.description: This property associates new names to the input point array names
PointArrayNames.label: Point Arrays

RowArrayNames.description: This property associates new names to the input row array names
RowArrayNames.label: Row Arrays

VertexArrayNames.description: This property associates new names to the input vertex array names
VertexArrayNames.label: Vertex Arrays

filters/AMRResampleFilter.short: Converts AMR data to a uniform grid
filters/AMRResampleFilter.long: Converts AMR data to a uniform grid
filters/AMRResampleFilter.description: This filter allows the user to specify a Region of Interest(ROI) within the AMR data-set and extract it as a uniform grid.
filters/AMRResampleFilter.selection: Converts AMR data to a uniform grid

Demand-Driven Mode.description: This property specifies whether the resampling filter will operate in demand-driven mode or not.
Demand-Driven Mode.label: Demand- Driven Mode

Input.description: This property specifies the input for this filter.
Input.label: Input

Max.description: This property sets the minimum 3-D coordinate location by which the particles will be filtered out.
Max.label: Max

Min.description: This property sets the minimum 3-D coordinate location by which the particles will be filtered out.
Min.label: Min

Number of Samples.description: Sets the number of samples in each dimension
Number of Samples.label: Number of Samples

NumberOfPartitions.description: Set the number of subdivisions for recursive coordinate bisection.
NumberOfPartitions.label: Number Of Partitions

TransferToNodes.description: This property specifies whether the solution will be transferred to the nodes of the extracted region or the cells.
TransferToNodes.label: Transfer To Nodes

filters/ResampleToImage.long: Sample attributes using a 3D image as probing mesh.

Input.description: This property specifies the dataset whose data will be probed
Input.label: Input

SamplingDimensions.description: How many linear samples we want along each axis
SamplingDimensions.label: Sampling Dimensions

UseInputBounds.description: Use input bounds or custom ones?
UseInputBounds.label: Use Input Bounds

filters/ResampleToLine.description: Resamples the input data set to a line.
filters/ResampleToLine.selection: Resamples the input data set to a line.

ComputeTolerance.description: Set whether to compute the tolerance or to use a user provided value.
ComputeTolerance.label: Compute Tolerance

Input.description: This property specifies which data set to resample.
Input.label: Input

PassCellArrays.description: When set the input cell data arrays are shallow copied to the output.
PassCellArrays.label: Pass Cell Arrays

PassFieldArrays.description: Set whether to pass the field-data arrays from the Input i.e. the input providing the geometry to the output.
PassFieldArrays.label: Pass Field Arrays

PassPartialArrays.description: When dealing with composite datasets, partial arrays are common i.e. data-arrays that are not available in all of the blocks. By default, this filter only passes those point and cell data-arrays that are available in all the blocks i.e. partial arrays are removed. When PassPartialArrays is turned on, this behavior is changed to take a union of all arrays present thus partial arrays are passed as well. However, for composite dataset input, this filter still produces a non-composite output. For all those locations in a block of where a particular data array is missing, this filter uses vtkMath::Nan() for double and float arrays, and 0 for all other types of arrays i.e int, char etc.
PassPartialArrays.label: Pass Partial Arrays

PassPointArrays.description: When set the input point data arrays are shallow copied to the output.
PassPointArrays.label: Pass Point Arrays

Point1.description: This property controls the coordinates of the first endpoint of the line.
Point1.label: Point1

Point2.description: This property controls the coordinates of the second endpoint of the line.
Point2.label: Point2

Resolution.description: This property sets the line resolution.
Resolution.label: Resolution

Tolerance.description: Set the tolerance to use for vtkDataSet::FindCell
Tolerance.label: Tolerance

filters/ResampleWithDataset.short: Sample data attributes at the points of a dataset.
filters/ResampleWithDataset.description: This filter takes two inputs - **Source Data Arrays**, and samples the point and cell values of this input onto the point locations of the **Destination Geometry** input. The output has the same structure as the **Destination Geometry** input, but its point data has the resampled values from the **Source Data Arrays**."
filters/ResampleWithDataset.selection: Sample data attributes at the points of a dataset.

CategoricalData.description: Control whether the source point data is to be treated as categorical. If the data is categorical, then the resultant data will be determined by a nearest neighbor interpolation scheme rather than by linear interpolation.
CategoricalData.label: Categorical Data

CellLocator.description: The cell locator to use for finding cells for probing.
CellLocator.label: Cell Locator

ComputeTolerance.description: Set whether to compute the tolerance or to use a user provided value. On by default.
ComputeTolerance.label: Compute Tolerance

DestinationMesh.description: This property specifies the dataset whose geometry will be used in determining positions to probe. The mesh comes from this dataset.
DestinationMesh.label: Destination Mesh

MarkBlankPointsAndCells.description: When set, points that did not get valid values during resampling, and cells containing such points, are marked as blank.
MarkBlankPointsAndCells.label: Mark Blank Points And Cells

PassCellArrays.description: When set the input's cell data arrays are shallow copied to the output.
PassCellArrays.label: Pass Cell Arrays

PassFieldArrays.description: Set whether to pass the field-data arrays from the Input i.e. the input providing the geometry to the output. On by default.
PassFieldArrays.label: Pass Field Arrays

PassPartialArrays.description: Set whether to partial data arrays from the Input i.e. the input providing the geometry to the output. Off by default.
PassPartialArrays.label: Pass Partial Arrays

PassPointArrays.description: When set the input's point data arrays are shallow copied to the output.
PassPointArrays.label: Pass Point Arrays

SnapToCellWithClosestPoint.description: Set whether to snap to the cell with the closest point, if no cell has been found while FindCell is executed. Note: This is useful only when the source is a vtkPointSet.
SnapToCellWithClosestPoint.label: Snap To Cell With Closest Point

SourceDataArrays.description: This property specifies the dataset from which to obtain probe values. The data attributes come from this dataset.
SourceDataArrays.label: Source Data Arrays

Tolerance.description: Set the tolerance to use for vtkDataSet::FindCell
Tolerance.label: Tolerance

UseImplicitArrays.description: **IMPORTANT:** this option only concerns Hyper Tree Grids sources (including composite source containing HTGs). If checked, the filter will optimize the space allocated to store the output probed values. This option will lower the memory consumption, especially if the probed source contains a lot of data arrays, at the cost of an increased computation time.
UseImplicitArrays.label: Reduce Output Memory Usage

textures/ImageTexture.description: This is a proxy for a vtkTexture which also includes an image file reader. This reader can read an image of client/data server or render server and then transmit it to the client/render server where it will be used for texturing.
textures/ImageTexture.selection: This is a proxy for a vtkTexture which also includes an image file reader. This reader can read an image of client/data server or render server and then transmit it to the client/render server where it will be used for texturing.

ColorMode.description: When color mode is Default, 8-bits textures is equivalent to Direct Scalars, while equivalent to Map Scalars for 16-bits textures. In the case of Map Scalars, all the values are mapped to a generic color map.
ColorMode.label: Color Mode

FileName.description: Set the name of image file to load.
FileName.label: File Name

Mode.description: Set the mode in which image data is read.
Mode.label: Mode

TrivialProducerKey.description: Set the key used to locate the image data object on the server.
TrivialProducerKey.label: Trivial Producer Key

lookup_tables/PVLookupTable.selection: Define a native colour lookup resource for declared representations or writer resource ports.

AboveRangeColor.description: Set the color to use when a data value is above the range of the color map.
AboveRangeColor.label: Above Range Color

AnnotationsInitialized.description: Set to 1 to indicate that the annotations have been initialized.
AnnotationsInitialized.label: Annotations Initialized

AutomaticDataHistogramComputation.description: Proxy only property used by the ColorOpacityWidget to know if the data histogram should be automatically computed
AutomaticDataHistogramComputation.label: Automatic Data Histogram Computation

AutomaticRescaleRangeMode.description: Choose whether and how to automatically rescale the color map range. "Never" means the color map range will never be changed. "Grow and update on 'Apply'" will expand the range to contain the union of the current range and the range of the current data source. "Grow and update every timestep" will expand the range to contain the union of the current range and the range of the current data source when the timestep is changed. "Clamp and update every timestep" will update the color map range to the current source data range.
AutomaticRescaleRangeMode.label: Automatic Rescale Range Mode

BelowRangeColor.description: Set the color to use when a data value is below the range of the color map.
BelowRangeColor.label: Below Range Color

ColorSpace.description: The color space used for interpolation: RGB, HSV, Lab (CIELAB), or Diverging. In HSV mode, if HSVWrap is on, it will take the shortest path in Hue (going back through 0 if that is the shortest way around the hue circle) whereas if HSVWrap is off it will not go through 0 (in order the match the current functionality of vtkLookupTable). Diverging is a special mode where colors will pass through white when interpolating between two saturated colors. In Lab/CIEDE2000 mode, it will take the shortest path in the Lab color space with respect to the CIE Delta E 2000 color distance measure. In Step mode, the color of an interval is the color of the second point of the interval.
ColorSpace.label: Color Space

DataHistogramNumberOfBins.description: Proxy only property used by the ColorOpacityWidget to know the number of bin to use to compute the data histogram
DataHistogramNumberOfBins.label: Data Histogram Number Of Bins

Discretize.description: When set, the color transfer function will comprise of discrete colors with number of discrete colors specified using NumberOfTableValues.
Discretize.label: Discretize

EnableOpacityMapping.description: When enabled, the opacity transfer function is used for rendering, if applicable.
EnableOpacityMapping.label: Enable Opacity Mapping

IndexedColors.description: Colors used when using IndexedLookup is true.
IndexedColors.label: Indexed Colors

IndexedLookup.description: When enabled, the color transfer function switches to indexed-lookup (categorical colors) mode.
IndexedLookup.label: Interpret Values As Categories

IndexedOpacities.description: Opacities used when using IndexedLookup is true.
IndexedOpacities.label: Indexed Opacities

NanColor.description: Set the color to use when NaN (not-a-number) is encountered.
NanColor.label: Nan Color

NanOpacity.description: Set the opacity to use when NaN (not-a-number) is encountered.
NanOpacity.label: Nan Opacity

NumberOfTableValues.description: When Discretize is set, this specifies the number of discrete colors that must be present in the transfer function.
NumberOfTableValues.label: Number Of Table Values

RGBPoints.description: Specify the control points that form the color-transfer-function. These are a list of 4-tuples of the form (x, r, g, b) where x is the data value, and r,g,b are three color components in the range [0,1].
RGBPoints.label: RGB Points

RescaleOnVisibilityChange.description: Flag indicating whether the color map data range should be updated when a representation's visibility changes.
RescaleOnVisibilityChange.label: Rescale On Visibility Change

ScalarRangeInitialized.description: Set to 1 to indicate that the scalar range has been initialized.
ScalarRangeInitialized.label: Scalar Range Initialized

ShowDataHistogram.description: Proxy only property used by the ColorOpacityWidget to know if the data histogram should be shown
ShowDataHistogram.label: Show Data Histogram

ShowIndexedColorActiveValues.description: When interpreting values as categories, enabling this option results in the display of only the 'active' categorical colors for values in the data range, i.e., values that exist in the source. You may need to click the 'Rescale to Data Range' button to update the active values that are displayed.
ShowIndexedColorActiveValues.label: Show Categorical Colors in Data Range Only

TransferFunction2D.description: Proxy property used by the ColorOpacityWidget to store a 2D transfer function (vtkImageData).
TransferFunction2D.label: Transfer Function2D

UseAboveRangeColor.description: Use special color to use when a data value is above the range of the color map.
UseAboveRangeColor.label: Use Above Range Color

UseBelowRangeColor.description: Use special color to use when a data value is below the range of the color map.
UseBelowRangeColor.label: Use Below Range Color

UseOpacityControlPointsFreehandDrawing.description: Proxy only property used by the ColorOpacityWidget to know if freehand drawing should be used
UseOpacityControlPointsFreehandDrawing.label: Use Opacity Control Points Freehand Drawing

Using2DTransferFunction.description: Proxy only property used by the ColorOpacityWidget to know if a 2D transfer function is being used.
Using2DTransferFunction.label: Using2D Transfer Function

UsingSeparateOpacityArray.description: Proxy only property used by the ColorOpacityWidget to know if a separate array is being used to map opacity in volume rendering.
UsingSeparateOpacityArray.label: Using Separate Opacity Array

piecewise_functions/PiecewiseFunction.selection: Define a scalar piecewise-function resource for declared transfer-function uses.

ScalarRangeInitialized.description: Set to 1 to indicate that the scalar range has been initialized.
ScalarRangeInitialized.label: Scalar Range Initialized

textures/Texture.selection: Define a native texture resource; inspect input image format and resource ownership.

transfer_2d_functions/TransferFunction2D.selection: Define a two-dimensional transfer-function resource; native rendering requirements apply.

AutomaticRescaleRangeMode.description: Choose whether and how to automatically rescale the color map range. "Never" means the color map range will never be changed. "Grow and update on 'Apply'" will expand the range to contain the union of the current range and the range of the current data source. "Grow and update every timestep" will expand the range to contain the union of the current range and the range of the current data source when the timestep is changed. "Clamp and update every timestep" will update the color map range to the current source data range.
AutomaticRescaleRangeMode.label: Automatic Rescale Range Mode

Boxes.description: Specify the box parameters for the 2D transfer function. These are a list of 8-tuples of the form (x, y, width, height, r, g, b, a) where (x, y) is the position i.e. the range-min of the box, (width, height) specify the dimensions of the box in the scalar units and (r, g, b, a) denote the color with maximum alpha of the box. The color and alpha components are in the range [0, 1].
Boxes.label: Boxes

OutputDimensions.description: The dimensions of the image that represents this 2D transfer function.
OutputDimensions.label: Output Dimensions

Range.description: The range of the X and Y axes of the transfer function. This is specified as a 4-tuple of the form (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax).
Range.label: Range

ScalarRangeInitialized.description: Set to 1 to indicate that the scalar range has been initialized.
ScalarRangeInitialized.label: Scalar Range Initialized

sources/ExodusRestartReader.short: Read Exodus files from simulation restarts.
sources/ExodusRestartReader.long: Reads collections of Exodus output files from simulations that were restarted.
sources/ExodusRestartReader.description: When a simulation that outputs exodus files is restarted, typically you get a new set of output files. When you read them in your visualization, you often want to string these file sets together as if it was one continuous dump of files. This reader allows you to specify a metadata file that will implicitly string the files together. This is a distributed reader.
sources/ExodusRestartReader.selection: Read Exodus files from simulation restarts.

FileName.description: This points to a special metadata file that lists the output files for each restart.
FileName.label: File Name

UseMetaFile.description: This hidden property must always be set to 1 for this proxy to work.
UseMetaFile.label: Use Meta File

AnimateVibrations.description: If this flag is on and HasModeShapes is also on, then this reader will report a continuous time range [0,1] and animate the displacements in a periodic sinusoid. If this flag is off and HasModeShapes is on, this reader ignores time. This flag has no effect if HasModeShapes is off.
AnimateVibrations.label: Animate Vibrations

ApplyDisplacements.description: Geometric locations can include displacements. When this option is on, the nodal positions are 'displaced' by the standard exodus displacement vector. If displacements are turned 'off', the user can explicitly add them by applying a warp filter.
ApplyDisplacements.label: Apply Displacements

DisplacementMagnitude.description: When displacements are being applied, they are scaled by this amount. Set to 1 for no scaling.
DisplacementMagnitude.label: Displacement Magnitude

EdgeBlocks.description: Use this property to select which blocks of edges should be loaded. All edges in the same block will have the same interpolant (linear, quadratic, etc.) and have the same variables defined over them.
EdgeBlocks.label: Edge Blocks

EdgeMapArrayStatus.description: Specify which maps defined over edges in the mesh should be loaded. An edge map is a renumbering of all the edges (across all the edge blocks of a file) from their offset in the file to some arbitrary integers, usually specifying a unique global ID across a set of files.
EdgeMapArrayStatus.label: Edge Map Array Status

EdgeSetArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the edges (across all edge blocks) in a file as sets in their own right. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per edge. The accompanying EdgeSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
EdgeSetArrayStatus.label: Edge Set Array Status

EdgeSetResultArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the edges (across all edge blocks) in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per edge. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the EdgeSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
EdgeSetResultArrayStatus.label: Edge Set Result Array Status

EdgeVariables.description: Use this property to select which variables defined over edges should be loaded. Edges are oriented boundaries of one or more higher-dimensional cells also present in the mesh. Edge variables specify a single value per entry in some edge block.
EdgeVariables.label: Edge Variables

ElementBlocks.description: Use this property to select which blocks of elements (cells) should be loaded. All elements (cells) in the same block will have the same interpolant (tetrahedral, triangular, trilinear hexahedral, etc.) and have the same variables defined over them.
ElementBlocks.label: Element Blocks

ElementMapArrayStatus.description: Specify which maps defined over elements (cells) in the mesh should be loaded. An element map is a renumbering of all the elements (across all the element blocks of a file) from their offset in the file to some arbitrary integers, usually specifying a unique global ID across a set of files. These are sometimes called new-style maps because they are specified differently than in older Exodus files, which only allowed a single element map.
ElementMapArrayStatus.label: Element Map Array Status

ElementSetArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the elements (across all element blocks) in a file as sets in their own right. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. Variables, such as feature classifiers, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per element. The accompanying ElementSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
ElementSetArrayStatus.label: Element Set Array Status

ElementSetResultArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the elements (across all element blocks) in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as feature classifiers, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per element. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the ElementSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
ElementSetResultArrayStatus.label: Element Set Result Array Status

ElementVariables.description: Use this property to select which variables defined over elements (cells) should be loaded. Element variables specify a single value per entry in some element block.
ElementVariables.label: Element Variables

FaceBlocks.description: Use this property to select which blocks of faces should be loaded. All faces in the same block will have the same interpolant (triangular, bilinear quadrilateral, etc.) and have the same variables defined over them.
FaceBlocks.label: Face Blocks

FaceMapArrayStatus.description: Specify which maps defined over faces in the mesh should be loaded. A face map is a renumbering of all the faces (across all the face blocks of a file) from their offset in the file to some arbitrary integers, usually specifying a unique global ID across a set of files.
FaceMapArrayStatus.label: Face Map Array Status

FaceSetArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the faces (across all face blocks) in a file as sets in their own right. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per face. The accompanying FaceSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
FaceSetArrayStatus.label: Face Set Array Status

FaceSetResultArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the faces (across all face blocks) in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per face. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the FaceSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
FaceSetResultArrayStatus.label: Face Set Result Array Status

FaceVariables.description: Use this property to select which variables defined over faces should be loaded. Faces are oriented boundaries of one or more higher-dimensional cells also present in the mesh. Face variables specify a single value per entry in some face block.
FaceVariables.label: Face Variables

FilePattern.description: This property contains a text string specifying the pattern used to load files. There are two parts to it: the prefix (%s) and the file number (%i). The format used is the same as that used for printf.
FilePattern.label: File Pattern

FilePrefix.description: This property specifies the file root used with the file pattern to format a file name. (See the File Pattern property).
FilePrefix.label: File Prefix

FileRange.description: This property controls the indices of the first and last files to be read.
FileRange.label: File Range

GenerateFileIdArray.description: Should each cell in the mesh be assigned an integer identifying the file it came from? If turned on, a cell variable named "FileId" should be present.
GenerateFileIdArray.label: Generate File Id Array

GenerateGlobalElementIdArray.description: Should the reader retrieve the first new-style element map, or if that is not present, the solitary old-style element map (which always exists but may be procedurally generated if it is not stored with the file)?
GenerateGlobalElementIdArray.label: Generate Global Element Id Array

GenerateGlobalNodeIdArray.description: Should the reader retrieve the first new-style node map, or if that is not present, the solitary old-style node map (which always exists but may be procedurally generated if it is not stored with the file)?
GenerateGlobalNodeIdArray.label: Generate Global Node Id Array

GenerateObjectIdCellArray.description: Specifies whether a variable named "ObjectId" should be created for each entry of each block and set being loaded and assigned the identifying number of the block or set, so that given a cell one can readily identify the block or set it came from. This is useful for coloring a mesh by block ID or set ID.
GenerateObjectIdCellArray.label: Generate Object Id Cell Array

GlobalVariables.description: Use this property to select which global (i.e., per-mesh) variables should be loaded. Global variables are stored as arrays in the field data of the reader's output.
GlobalVariables.label: Global Variables

HasModeShapes.description: Some simulations overload the Exodus time steps to represent mode shapes. In this case, it does not make sense to iterate over the "time steps", because they are not meant to be played in order. Rather, each represents the vibration at a different "mode." Setting the value of this property to 1 changes the semantics of the reader to not report the time steps to downstream filters.
HasModeShapes.label: Has Mode Shapes

ModeShape.description: Specify which mode shape to animate when HasModeShapes is on.
ModeShape.label: Mode Shape

NodeMapArrayStatus.description: Specify which maps defined over nodes (points) in the mesh should be loaded. A node map is a renumbering of all the points in a file from their offset in the file to some arbitrary integers, usually specifying a unique global ID across a set of files. These are sometimes called new-style maps because they are specified differently than in older Exodus files, which only allowed a single node map.
NodeMapArrayStatus.label: Node Map Array Status

NodeSetArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the nodes (points) in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per node. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. The accompanying NodeSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
NodeSetArrayStatus.label: Node Set Array Status

NodeSetResultArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the nodes (points) in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per node. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the NodeSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
NodeSetResultArrayStatus.label: Node Set Result Array Status

PointVariables.description: Use this property to select which nodal (i.e., per-point) variables should be loaded.
PointVariables.label: Point Variables

SideSetArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the of all the elements in a file as sets in their own right. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per side. For example, a hexahedron has 18 sides: 6 faces and 12 edges. Any of these sides may be individually called out in a set and assigned a result value. The accompanying SideSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
SideSetArrayStatus.label: Side Set Array Status

SideSetResultArrayStatus.description: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the of all the elements in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per side. For example, a hexahedron has 18 sides: 6 faces and 12 edges. Any of these sides may be individually called out in a set and assigned a result value. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the SideSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
SideSetResultArrayStatus.label: Side Set Result Array Status

UseLegacyBlockNamesWithElementTypes.description: In previous versions, the reader added the type of elements in the block to the block name when no name was provided for the block. This has issues with consistency when naming blocks across ranks for partitioned files. Hence we no longer do that. For legacy pipelines, one can enable the old behavior by setting this flag to true.
UseLegacyBlockNamesWithElementTypes.label: Use Legacy Block Names With Element Types

XMLFileName.description: This property specifies the name of an XML file containing part and material descriptions and a mapping to element blocks.
XMLFileName.label: XML File Name

sources/SPCTHRestartReader.short: Read SPCTH files from simulation restarts.
sources/SPCTHRestartReader.long: Reads collections of SPCTH files from simulations that were restarted.
sources/SPCTHRestartReader.description: When a CTH simulation is restarted, typically you get a new set of output files. When you read them in your visualization, you often want to string these file sets together as if it was one continuous dump of files. This reader allows you to specify a metadata file that will implicitly string the files together. This is a distributed reader.
sources/SPCTHRestartReader.selection: Read SPCTH files from simulation restarts.

FileName.description: This points to a special metadata file that lists the output files for each restart.
FileName.label: File Name

UseMetaFile.description: This hidden property must always be set to 1 for this proxy to work.
UseMetaFile.label: Use Meta File

CellArrayStatus.description: This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
CellArrayStatus.label: Cell Arrays

DistributeFiles.description: In parallel mode, if this property is set to 1, the reader will distribute files or blocks.
DistributeFiles.label: Distribute Files

DownConvertVolumeFraction.description: If this property is set to 0, the type of the volume fraction is float; is set to 1, the type is unsigned char.
DownConvertVolumeFraction.label: Down Convert Volume Fraction

GenerateActiveBlockArray.description: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the active status of a block.
GenerateActiveBlockArray.label: Generate Active Block Array

GenerateBlockIdArray.description: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores a unique blockId for each block.
GenerateBlockIdArray.label: Generate Block Id Array

GenerateLevelArray.description: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the level of each block.
GenerateLevelArray.label: Generate Level Array

GenerateMarkers.description: If this property is set to 1, a second output will be created using the markers data stored in the file.
GenerateMarkers.label: Generate Markers

GenerateTracers.description: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the coordinates of any tracers.
GenerateTracers.label: Generate Tracers

filters/ReverseSense.short: Reverse the ordering of vertices in polygons.
filters/ReverseSense.description: This filter reverses vertex ordering or normals for cells. In graphics 2d cells have a notion of front or back face. If you use the right hand rule and wind the vertices of a cell counter-clockwise (how your right fungers coil) then the front face is in the direction of your thumb (the normal aligns with your right thumb). If you need to reverse the normals, or change the winding order of a polydata this filter can be used.
filters/ReverseSense.selection: Reverse the ordering of vertices in polygons.

Input.description: Set the input to the ReverseSense filter.
Input.label: Input

ReverseCells.description: Flag controls whether to reverse cell ordering.
ReverseCells.label: Reverse Cells

ReverseNormals.description: Flag controls whether to reverse normal orientation.
ReverseNormals.label: Reverse Normals

filters/RibbonFilter.long: This filter generates ribbon surface from lines.  It is useful for displaying streamlines.
filters/RibbonFilter.description: The Ribbon filter creates ribbons from the lines in the input data set. This filter is useful for visualizing streamlines. Both the input and output of this filter are polygonal data. The input data set must also have at least one point-centered vector array.

Angle.description: The value of this property specifies the offset angle (in degrees) of the ribbon from the line normal.
Angle.label: Angle

DefaultNormal.description: The value of this property specifies the normal to use when the UseDefaultNormal property is set to 1 or the input contains no vector array (SelectInputVectors property).
DefaultNormal.label: Default Normal

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Ribbon filter.
Input.label: Input

SelectInputScalars.description: The value of this property indicates the name of the input scalar array used by this filter. The width of the ribbons will be varied based on the values in the specified array if the value of the Width property is 1.
SelectInputScalars.label: Scalars

SelectInputVectors.description: The value of this property indicates the name of the input vector array used by this filter. If the UseDefaultNormal property is set to 0, the normal vectors for the ribbons come from the specified vector array.
SelectInputVectors.label: Vectors

UseDefaultNormal.description: If this property is set to 0, and the input contains no vector array, then default ribbon normals will be generated (DefaultNormal property); if a vector array has been set (SelectInputVectors property), the ribbon normals will be set from the specified array. If this property is set to 1, the default normal (DefaultNormal property) will be used, regardless of whether the SelectInputVectors property has been set.
UseDefaultNormal.label: Use Default Normal

VaryWidth.description: If this property is set to 1, the ribbon width will be scaled according to the scalar array specified in the SelectInputScalars property. Toggle the variation of ribbon width with scalar value.
VaryWidth.label: Vary Width

Width.description: If the VaryWidth property is set to 1, the value of this property is the minimum ribbon width. If the VaryWidth property is set to 0, the value of this property is half the width of the ribbon.
Width.label: Width

filters/RotationalExtrusionFilter.short: Generates a swept surface using a rotational path.
filters/RotationalExtrusionFilter.long: This filter generates a swept surface while translating the input along a circular path.
filters/RotationalExtrusionFilter.description: The Rotational Extrusion filter forms a surface by rotating the input about the Z axis. This filter is intended to operate on 2D polygonal data. It produces polygonal output.
filters/RotationalExtrusionFilter.selection: Generates a swept surface using a rotational path.

Angle.description: This property specifies the angle of rotation in degrees. The surface is swept from 0 to the value of this property.
Angle.label: Angle

Capping.description: If this property is set to 1, the open ends of the swept surface will be capped with a copy of the input dataset. This works property if the input is a 2D surface composed of filled polygons. If the input dataset is a closed solid (e.g., a sphere), then either two copies of the dataset will be drawn or no surface will be drawn. No surface is drawn if either this property is set to 0 or if the two surfaces would occupy exactly the same 3D space (i.e., the Angle property's value is a multiple of 360, and the values of the Translation and DeltaRadius properties are 0).
Capping.label: Capping

DeltaRadius.description: The value of this property specifies the change in radius during the sweep process.
DeltaRadius.label: Delta Radius

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Rotational Extrusion filter.
Input.label: Input

Resolution.description: The value of this property controls the number of intermediate node points used in performing the sweep (rotating from 0 degrees to the value specified by the Angle property.
Resolution.label: Resolution

RotationAxis.description: The values of this property set the direction of the axis around which the rotation is done.
RotationAxis.label: Rotation Axis

Translation.description: The value of this property specifies the total amount of translation along the rotation axis during the sweep process. Specifying a non-zero value for this property allows you to create a corkscrew (value of DeltaRadius > 0) or spring effect.
Translation.label: Translation

sources/Ruler.long: This is a line source that can be used to measure distance between two points
sources/Ruler.description: The ruler can be used to interactively (using a 3D widget) or manually (using the entries on the user interface) specify two points and then determine the distance between the two points. To place points on the surface of any dataset, one can use the 'p' key shortcut.

Point1.description: This property controls the coordinates of the first endpoint of the line.
Point1.label: Point1

Point2.description: This property controls the coordinates of the second endpoint of the line.
Point2.label: Point2

FileName.description: Specify the file name.
FileName.label: File Name

sources/SEPReader.long: This reader takes a .H file that points to a .H@ file and contains all the information to interpret the raw data in the .H@ file.

ExtentSplitMode.description: This property specifies the extent mode.
ExtentSplitMode.label: Extent Split Mode

FileName.description: This property specifies the file name for the SEP reader.
FileName.label: File Name

OutputGridDimension.description: This property specifies the dimension of the output data set.
OutputGridDimension.label: Output Grid Dimension

sources/SLACReader.short: A reader for a data format used by       Omega3p, Tau3p, and several other tools used at the Standford       Linear Accelerator Center (SLAC)
sources/SLACReader.description: A reader for a data format used by Omega3p, Tau3p, and several other tools used at the Standford Linear Accelerator Center (SLAC). The underlying format uses NetCDF to store arrays, but also imposes several conventions to form an unstructured grid of elements. This is a distributed reader.
sources/SLACReader.selection: A reader for a data format used by       Omega3p, Tau3p, and several other tools used at the Standford       Linear Accelerator Center (SLAC)

FrequencyScale.description: Sets the scale factor for each mode. By default, each scale factor is set to 1.
FrequencyScale.label: Frequency Scale

MeshFileName.description: The name of the mesh file to load.
MeshFileName.label: Mesh File Name

ModeFileName.description: The name of the mode files to load. The points in the mode file should be the same as the mesh file.
ModeFileName.label: Mode File Name

PhaseShift.description: Sets the phase offset for each mode. By default, shift is set to 0.
PhaseShift.label: Phase Shift

ReadExternalSurface.description: If on, read the external surfaces of the data set.
ReadExternalSurface.label: Read External Surface

ReadInternalVolume.description: If on, read the internal volume of the data set.
ReadInternalVolume.label: Read Internal Volume

ReadMidpoints.description: If on, reads midpoint information for external surfaces and builds quadratic surface triangles.
ReadMidpoints.label: Read Midpoints

TimeRange.description: This magic property sends time range information to the animation panel. ParaView uses this information to set the range of time for the animation. This property is important for when there are no timesteps but you still want to give ParaView a range of values to use.
TimeRange.label: Time Range

TimestepValues.description: This magic property sends time information to the animation panel. ParaView will then automatically set up the animation to visit the time steps defined in the file.
TimestepValues.label: Timestep Values

FileName.description: A list of files to be read in a time series.
FileName.label: File Name

filters/SPHDatasetInterpolator.description: This filter uses SPH (smooth particle hydrodynamics) kernels to interpolate a data source onto an input structure. For example, while the data source is a set of particles, the data from these particles can be interpolated onto an input volume. Then the output (which consists of the input structure plus interpolated data) can then be visualized using classical visualization techniques such as isocontouring, slicing, heat maps and so on.
filters/SPHDatasetInterpolator.selection: This filter uses SPH (smooth particle hydrodynamics) kernels to interpolate a data source onto an input structure. For example, while the data source is a set of particles, the data from these particles can be interpolated onto an input volume. Then the output (which consists of the input structure plus interpolated data) can then be visualized using classical visualization techniques such as isocontouring, slicing, heat maps and so on.

ComputeShepardSum.description: Indicate whether to compute the summation of Shepard coefficients. In the interior of a SPH point cloud, the Shephard summation value should be ~1.0. Towards the boundary, the Shepard summation is less than 1.0. If ComputeShepardSum is specified, then the output will contain an array of summed Shepard weights for each output point.
ComputeShepardSum.label: Compute Shepard Sum

CutoffArray.description: Specify the Cutoff array name. If not specified, then the radius at each point will be computed as cutoff factor * smoothing length at a each point.
CutoffArray.label: Cutoff Array

DensityArray.description: Specify the density array name. This is required in computation. If not specified the code will error out.
DensityArray.label: Density Array

DerivativeArrays.description: Specify the arrays whose derivative is to be taken. If the name of the array is "derivArray" this will produce an output array with the name "derivArray_deriv" (after filter execution).
DerivativeArrays.label: Derivative Arrays

ExcludedArrays.description: Specify arrays which are to be excluded from the interpolation process.
ExcludedArrays.label: Excluded Arrays

Input.description: The data source to be interpolated onto the *Source*.
Input.label: Input

MassArray.description: Specify the mass array name. If not specified, then the mass at each point will be computed from the density and local (spherical) volume at a each point.
MassArray.label: Mass Array

NullPointsStrategy.description: Specify a strategy to use when encountering a "null" point during the interpolation process. Null points occur when the local neighborhood (of nearby points to interpolate from) is empty. If the strategy is set to MaskPoints, then an output array is created that marks points as being valid (=1) or null (invalid =0) (and the NullValue is set as well). If the strategy is set to NullValue, then the output data value(s) are set to the NullPoint value (specified in the output point data).
NullPointsStrategy.label: Null Points Strategy

NullValue.description: Specify the null point value. When a null point is encountered then all components of each null tuple are set to this value. By default the null value is set to zero.
NullValue.label: Null Value

PassCellArrays.description: Indicate whether to shallow copy the input cell data arrays to the output.
PassCellArrays.label: Pass Cell Arrays

PassFieldArrays.description: Indicate whether to shallow copy the input field data arrays to the output.
PassFieldArrays.label: Pass Field Arrays

PassPointArrays.description: Indicate whether to shallow copy the input point data arrays to the output.
PassPointArrays.label: Pass Point Arrays

ShepardSumArrayName.description: If ComputeShepardSum is on, then an array is generated with name ShepardSumArrayName for each input point. This vtkFloatArray is placed into the output of the filter, and NullPoints have value =0.0. The default name is "Shepard Summation".
ShepardSumArrayName.label: Shepard Sum Array Name

Source.description: The data source that provides the structure to be interpolated on.
Source.label: Source

ValidPointsMaskArrayName.description: If the NullPointsStrategy is "Mask Points", then an array is generated for each input point. This vtkCharArray is placed into the output of the filter, with a non-zero value for a valid point, and zero otherwise. The name of this masking array is specified here.
ValidPointsMaskArrayName.label: Valid Points Mask Array Name

filters/SPHInterpolatorBase.description: This filter uses SPH (smooth particle hydrodynamics) kernels to interpolate a data source onto an input structure. For example, while the data source is a set of particles, the data from these particles can be interpolated onto an input object such as a line, plane or volume. Then the output (which consists of the input structure plus interpolated data) can then be visualized using classical visualization techniques such as isocontouring, slicing, heat maps and so on.
filters/SPHInterpolatorBase.selection: This filter uses SPH (smooth particle hydrodynamics) kernels to interpolate a data source onto an input structure. PassFieldArrays.label: Pass Field Arrays

PassPointArrays.description: Indicate whether to shallow copy the input point data arrays to the output.
PassPointArrays.label: Pass Point Arrays

ShepardSumArrayName.description: If ComputeShepardSum is on, then an array is generated with name ShepardSumArrayName for each input point. This vtkFloatArray is placed into the output of the filter, and NullPoints have value =0.0. The default name is "Shepard Summation".
ShepardSumArrayName.label: Shepard Sum Array Name

Source.description: The data source that provides the structure to be interpolated on.
Source.label: Source

ValidPointsMaskArrayName.description: If the NullPointsStrategy is "Mask Points", then an array is generated for each input point. This vtkCharArray is placed into the output of the filter, with a non-zero value for a valid point, and zero otherwise. The name of this masking array is specified here.
ValidPointsMaskArrayName.label: Valid Points Mask Array Name

filters/SPHPlaneInterpolator.description: This filter uses SPH (smooth particle hydrodynamics) kernels to interpolate a data source onto an input structure. For example, while the data source is a set of particles, the data from these particles can be interpolated onto an input plane. Then the output (which consists of the input structure plus interpolated data) can then be visualized using classical visualization techniques such as isocontouring, slicing, heat maps and so on.
filters/SPHPlaneInterpolator.selection: This filter uses SPH (smooth particle hydrodynamics) kernels to interpolate a data source onto an input structure. For example, while the data source is a set of particles, the data from these particles can be interpolated onto an input plane. Then the output (which consists of the input structure plus interpolated data) can then be visualized using classical visualization techniques such as isocontouring, slicing, heat maps and so on.

ComputeShepardSum.description: Indicate whether to compute the summation of Shepard coefficients. In the interior of a SPH point cloud, the Shephard summation value should be ~1.0. Towards the boundary, the Shepard summation is less than 1.0. If ComputeShepardSum is specified, then the output will contain an array of summed Shepard weights for each output point.
ComputeShepardSum.label: Compute Shepard Sum

DensityArray.description: Specify the density array name. This is required in computation. If not specified the code will error out.
DensityArray.label: Density Array

DerivativeArrays.description: Specify the arrays whose derivative is to be taken. If the name of the array is "derivArray" this will produce an output array with the name "derivArray_deriv" (after filter execution).
DerivativeArrays.label: Derivative Arrays

ExcludedArrays.description: Specify arrays which are to be excluded from the interpolation process.
ExcludedArrays.label: Excluded Arrays

Input.description: The data source to be interpolated onto the *Source*.
Input.label: Input

MassArray.description: Specify the mass array name. If not specified, then the mass at each point will be computed from the density and local (spherical) volume at a each point.
MassArray.label: Mass Array

NullPointsStrategy.description: Specify a strategy to use when encountering a "null" point during the interpolation process. Null points occur when the local neighborhood (of nearby points to interpolate from) is empty. If the strategy is set to MaskPoints, then an output array is created that marks points as being valid (=1) or null (invalid =0) (and the NullValue is set as well). If the strategy is set to NullValue, then the output data value(s) are set to the NullPoint value (specified in the output point data).
NullPointsStrategy.label: Null Points Strategy

NullValue.description: Specify the null point value. When a null point is encountered then all components of each null tuple are set to this value. By default the null value is set to zero.
NullValue.label: Null Value

PassCellArrays.label: Pass Cell Arrays

PassFieldArrays.description: Indicate whether to shallow copy the input field data arrays to the output.
PassFieldArrays.label: Pass Field Arrays

PassPointArrays.description: Indicate whether to shallow copy the input point data arrays to the output.
PassPointArrays.label: Pass Point Arrays
