sources/STEPReader.description: The STEP reader reads .step, .stp file extensions.

FileNames.description: The list of files to be read by the reader. If more than one file is specified, the reader will switch to file series mode in which it will pretend that it can support time and provide one file per time step.
FileNames.label: File Names

AngularDeflection.description: Limits the angle between two subsequent segments.
AngularDeflection.label: Angular Deflection

LinearDeflection.description: Limits the distance between a curve and the resulting tesselation.
LinearDeflection.label: Linear Deflection

ReadWire.description: Determines if 1D cells will be read. If enabled, surface boundaries are read.
ReadWire.label: Read Wire

RelativeDeflection.description: Determines if the deflection values are relative to object size.
RelativeDeflection.label: Relative Deflection

sources/stlreader.long: Reads ASCII or binary stereo lithography (STL) files.
sources/stlreader.description: The STL reader reads ASCII or binary stereo lithography (STL) files. The expected file extension is .stl. The output of this reader is a polygonal dataset. This reader also supports file series.

FileNames.description: The list of files to be read by the reader. If more than one file is specified, the reader will switch to file series mode in which it will pretend that it can support time and provide one file per time step.
FileNames.label: File Names

filters/ScatterPlot.short: Creates a scatter plot from a dataset.
filters/ScatterPlot.long: Creates a scatter plot from a dataset.
filters/ScatterPlot.description: This filter creates a scatter plot from a dataset.
filters/ScatterPlot.selection: Creates a scatter plot from a dataset.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the filter.
Input.label: Input

sources/SegY Reader.description: SEG-Y Reader reads SEG-Y data files. We create a Structured Grid for 2.5D SEG-Y and 3D data. If we set the StructuredGrid option to false we create a Image Data for 3D data. This saves memory and may speed-up certain algorithms, but the position and the shape of the data may not be correct. The axes for the data are: crossline, inline, depth.

FileName.description: This property specifies the file name for the SEG-Y reader.
FileName.label: File Name

Force2D.description: Specify if we create a Structured Grid even when the data is SEG-Y 3D. Note this consumes more memory but it shows the precise location for each point and the correct shape of the data. The default value is true. If we set this option to false we create an Image Data for a SEG-Y 3D dataset. Specify if we should we force the data to be interpreted as a 2D dataset. It may be a 2D sheet through 3D space. When this is turned on we ignore the cross line and line values and instead build a 2D data by processing and connecting the traces in order from first to last. The output will be a Structured Grid.
Force2D.label: Force 2D

StructuredGrid.description: Specify if we create a Structured Grid even when the data is SEG-Y 3D. Note this consumes more memory but it shows the precise location for each point and the correct shape of the data. The default value is true. If we set this option to false we create an Image Data for a SEG-Y 3D dataset.
StructuredGrid.label: Structured Grid

VerticalCRS.description: Specify whether the vertical coordinates in the SEG-Y file are heights (positive up) or depths (positive down). By default, the vertical coordinates are treated as heights (i.e. positive up). This means that the Z-axis of the dataset goes from 0 (surface) to -ve depth (last sample). Note. As per the SEG-Y rev 2.0 specification, this information is defined in the Location Data Stanza of the Extended Textual Header. However, as of this revision, SegYReader does not support reading the extended textual header.
VerticalCRS.label: Vertical CRS

XCoordByte.description: Specify X and Y byte positions for custom XYCoordinateMode. By default, XCoordByte = 73, YCoordByte = 77 i.e. source xy.
XCoordByte.label: X Coord Byte

XYCoordMode.description: Specify whether to use source x/y coordinates or CDP coordinates or custom byte positions for data position in the SEG-Y trace header. Defaults to source x/y coordinates. As per SEG-Y rev 2.0 specification: - Source XY coordinate bytes = (73, 77) - CDP XY coordinate bytes = (181, 185)
XYCoordMode.label: XY Coord Mode

YCoordByte.description: Specify X and Y byte positions for custom XYCoordinateMode. By default, XCoordByte = 73, YCoordByte = 77 i.e. source xy.
YCoordByte.label: Y Coord Byte

sources/SelectionQuerySource.selection: Create a query selection. ParaView evaluates query text with Python eval when the selection is extracted (vtkPythonSelector, paraview.detail.calculator.compute), so Schemaxis accepts only a closed structured query, generates the text itself and rejects authored query text.

Assembly.description: Select which assembly is used when specify selectors to choose blocks to show for composite datasets.
Assembly.label: Assembly

ContainingCells.description: When field type is POINT, this controls whether single vertex cells will be produced for each selected point, or whether the cells that contain each selected point will be produced. When field type is CELL this has no effect.
ContainingCells.label: Containing Cells

ElementType.description: Select the type of elements to select.
ElementType.label: Element Type

InsideOut.description: When this property is false the selection describes everything that should be extracted. When this is true the selection describes everything that should NOT be extracted.
InsideOut.label: Inside Out

NumberOfLayers.description: Specify the number of layers of connected elements to include in the selection.
NumberOfLayers.label: Number Of Layers

RemoveIntermediateLayers.description: When using NumberOfLayers, this controls if intermediate layers are removes or not. Default is false.
RemoveIntermediateLayers.label: Remove Intermediate Layers

RemoveSeed.description: When using NumberOfLayers, this controls if the initial seed selection is remove or not. Default is false.
RemoveSeed.label: Remove Seed

Selectors.description: For composite datasets, specify selectors to limit the view to a chosen subset of blocks.
Selectors.label: Selectors

sources/SelectionSourceBase.description: Internal proxy used to define the common API for Selection Source proxies. Do not use.
sources/SelectionSourceBase.selection: Internal proxy used to define the common API for Selection Source proxies. Do not use.

ContainingCells.description: When field type is POINT, this controls whether single vertex cells will be produced for each selected point, or whether the cells that contain each selected point will be produced. When field type is CELL this has no effect.
ContainingCells.label: Containing Cells

FieldType.description: The location of the array the selection came from (e.g. point, cell).
FieldType.label: Field Type

InsideOut.description: When this property is false the selection describes everything that should be extracted. When this is true the selection describes everything that should NOT be extracted.
InsideOut.label: Inside Out

NumberOfLayers.description: Specify the number of layers of connected elements to include in the selection.
NumberOfLayers.label: Number Of Layers

RemoveIntermediateLayers.description: When using NumberOfLayers, this controls if intermediate layers are removes or not. Default is false.
RemoveIntermediateLayers.label: Remove Intermediate Layers

RemoveSeed.description: When using NumberOfLayers, this controls if the initial seed selection is remove or not. Default is false.
RemoveSeed.label: Remove Seed

filters/ShrinkFilter.long: This filter shrinks each input cell so they pull away from their neighbors.
filters/ShrinkFilter.description: The Shrink filter causes the individual cells of a dataset to break apart from each other by moving each cell's points toward the centroid of the cell. The centroid of a cell is the average position of its points. This filter operates on any type of dataset and produces unstructured grid output.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Shrink filter.
Input.label: Input

ShrinkFactor.description: The value of this property determines how far the points will move. A value of 0 positions the points at the centroid of the cell. A value of 1 leaves them at their original positions.
ShrinkFactor.label: Shrink Factor

filters/Cut.long: This filter slices a data set with a plane. Slicing is similar to a contour. It creates surfaces from volumes and lines from surfaces.
filters/Cut.description: This filter extracts the portion of the input dataset that lies along the specified plane. The Slice filter takes any type of dataset or hyper tree grid as input. The output of this filter is polygonal data.

ContourValues.description: The values in this property specify a list of current offset values. This can be used to create multiple slices with different centers. Each entry represents a new slice with its center shifted by the offset value. The 'Values Range' information is the range based on the global bounding box, not necessarily on the current slice geometry configuration.
ContourValues.label: Slice Offset Values

CutFunction.description: This property sets the parameters of the slice function.
CutFunction.label: Slice Type

HyperTreeGridImplicitFunction.description: This property sets the parameters of the slice function.
HyperTreeGridImplicitFunction.label: Hyper Tree Grid Slicer

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Slice filter.
Input.label: Input

Locator.description: This property specifies which incremental point locator to use for handling duplicate/coincident points.
Locator.label: Point Merge Method

PreserveInputCells.description: This parameter controls whether to extract the entire cells that are sliced by the region or just extract a triangulated surface of that region.
PreserveInputCells.label: Crinkle slice

SetDual.description: If checked, uses the dual of the hyper tree grid.
SetDual.label: Use Dual

Triangulate the slice.description: This parameter controls whether to produce triangles in the output.
Triangulate the slice.label: Triangulate the slice

filters/SliceAlongPolyLine.short: Slice along the surface defined by sweeping a polyline parallel to the z-axis.
filters/SliceAlongPolyLine.long: Slice along the surface defined by sweeping a polyline parallel to the z-axis.
filters/SliceAlongPolyLine.description: The Slice Along PolyLine filter is similar to the Slice Filter except that it slices along a surface that is defined by sweeping the input polyline parallel to the z-axis. Explained another way: take a laser cutter and move it so that it hits every point on the input polyline while keeping it parallel to the z-axis. The surface cut from the input dataset is the result.
filters/SliceAlongPolyLine.selection: Slice along the surface defined by sweeping a polyline parallel to the z-axis.

PolyLine.description: Set the polyline to slice along.
PolyLine.label: Poly Line

Tolerance.description: The threshold used internally to determine correspondence between the polyline and the output slice. If the output has sections missing, increasing this value may help.
Tolerance.label: Tolerance

filters/GenericCut.short: Cut datasets with planes or spheres.
filters/GenericCut.long: This filter cuts a data set with a plane or sphere.  Cutting is similar to a contour.  It creates surfaces from volumes and lines from surfaces.
filters/GenericCut.description: The Generic Cut filter extracts the portion of the input data set that lies along the specified plane or sphere. From the Cut Function menu, you can select whether cutting will be performed with a plane or a sphere. The appropriate 3D widget (plane widget or sphere widget) will be displayed. The parameters of the cut function can be specified interactively using the 3D widget or manually using the traditional user interface controls. Instructions for using these 3D widgets and their corresponding user interfaces are found in section 7.4. By default, the cut lies on the specified plane or sphere. Using the Cut Offset Values portion of the interface, it is also possible to cut the data set at some offset from the original cut function. The Cut Offset Values are in the spatial units of the data set. To add a single offset, select the value from the New Value slider in the Add value portion of the interface and click the Add button, or press Enter. To instead add several evenly spaced offsets, use the controls in the Generate range of values section. Select the number of offsets to generate using the Number of Values slider. The Range slider controls the interval in which to generate the offsets. Once the number of values and range have been selected, click the Generate button. The new offsets will be added to the Offset Values list. To delete a value from the Cut Offset Values list, select the value and click the Delete button. (If no value is selected, the last value in the list will be removed.) Clicking the Delete All button removes all the values in the list. The Generic Cut filter takes a generic dataset as input. Use the Input menu to choose a data set to cut. The output of this filter is polygonal data.
filters/GenericCut.selection: Cut datasets with planes or spheres.

ContourValues.description: The values in this property specify a list of current offset values. This can be used to create multiple slices with different centers. Each entry represents a new slice with its center shifted by the offset value.
ContourValues.label: Slice Offset Values

CutFunction.description: Set the parameters to the implicit function used for cutting.
CutFunction.label: Cut Type

Input.description: Set the input to the Generic Cut filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/SliceWithPlane.long: This filter slices a data set with a plane. Slicing is similar to a contour. It creates surfaces from volumes and lines from surfaces. This filter is faster than the standard Slice filter.
filters/SliceWithPlane.description: This filter extracts the portion of the input dataset that lies along the specified plane. The Slice filter takes any type of dataset as input. This is a multithreaded implementation.

BuildHierarchy.description: If enabled and input is not an Image Data, Tree hierarchy will be computed, for a faster slice computation.
BuildHierarchy.label: Build Hierarchy

BuildTree.description: If enabled and input is not an Image Data, Sphere Tree will be computed, for a faster slice computation.
BuildTree.label: Build Tree

ComputeNormals.description: If enabled, compute the normal on each cell. Since all output cells are coplanar, the normal generated is simply the normal of the plane used to slice with. By default, computing of normals is disabled.
ComputeNormals.label: Compute Normals

GeneratePolygons.description: If enabled and input is a vtkImageData, vtkStructuredGrid or vtkRectilinearGrid, output slice will consist of polygons instead of only triangles.
GeneratePolygons.label: Generate Polygons

Input.description: This property specifies the input of the slice filter.
Input.label: Input

InterpolateAttributes.description: If enabled, interpolate attribute data. By default this is enabled. Point data is always interpolated. Cell data is transferred unless input is an image data.
InterpolateAttributes.label: Interpolate Attributes

MergePoints.description: This parameter controls whether to merge duplicated points in the slice.
MergePoints.label: Merge duplicated points in the slice

Plane.description: This property sets the parameters of the plane function.
Plane.label: Plane Type

SetDual.description: If checked, uses the dual of the hyper tree grid.
SetDual.label: Use Dual

UseNativeCutter.description: This property specifies whether the ParaView's generic dataset cutter is used instead of the specialized AMR cutter.
UseNativeCutter.label: Use Native Cutter

filters/SmoothPolyDataFilter.short: Smooth a polygonal surface without adding more points.
filters/SmoothPolyDataFilter.long: This filter smooths a polygonal surface by iteratively moving points toward their neighbors.
filters/SmoothPolyDataFilter.description: The Smooth filter operates on a polygonal data set by iteratively adjusting the position of the points using Laplacian smoothing. (Because this filter only adjusts point positions, the output data set is also polygonal.) This results in better-shaped cells and more evenly distributed points. The Convergence slider limits the maximum motion of any point. It is expressed as a fraction of the length of the diagonal of the bounding box of the data set. If the maximum point motion during a smoothing iteration is less than the Convergence value, the smoothing operation terminates.
filters/SmoothPolyDataFilter.selection: Smooth a polygonal surface without adding more points.

Convergence.description: The value of this property limits the maximum motion of any point. It is expressed as a fraction of the length of the diagonal of the bounding box of the input dataset. If the maximum point motion during a smoothing iteration is less than the value of this property, the smoothing operation terminates.
Convergence.label: Convergence

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Smooth filter.
Input.label: Input

NumberOfIterations.description: This property sets the maximum number of smoothing iterations to perform. More iterations produce better smoothing.
NumberOfIterations.label: Number of Iterations

filters/SpatioTemporalHarmonics.description: The Spatio Temporal Harmonics Attribute filter adds an array for point data. The values are computed for each point with the harmonics defined in the filter. Harmonics are defined by their amplitude, temporal frequency, wave vector, and phase.

Harmonics.description: This property defines the harmonics that will be computed and summed on each point. Default values are only example values, that would make sense for a dataset of geometrical bounds [-10,10,-10,10,-10,10] and time values greater than or equal to 0 and less than 2*Pi.
Harmonics.label: Harmonics

sources/SpatioTemporalHarmonicsSource.short: Create a 3D uniform grid with a spatio-temporal harmonics array.
sources/SpatioTemporalHarmonicsSource.description: Creates a 3D uniform grid with point data. The values are computed for each point with the harmonics defined in the source. Harmonics are defined by their amplitude, temporal frequency, wave vector, and phase. The grid is defined by its extent.
sources/SpatioTemporalHarmonicsSource.selection: Create a 3D uniform grid with a spatio-temporal harmonics array.

Harmonics.description: This property defines the harmonics that will be computed and summed on each point. By default, it generates harmonics in each direction, with parameters adapted to the default extent.
Harmonics.label: Harmonics

TimeStepValuesToGenerate.description: This property specifies the timestep values to generate. When generating a range, make sure to remove the max value for the loop to avoid time value duplication (0 == 2*Pi). By default, it generates 20 timesteps from [0;2*Pi[ for data loop.
TimeStepValuesToGenerate.label: Time Step Values

WholeExtent.description: The six values in the property indicate the X, Y, and Z extent of the output data. The first two numbers are the minimum and maximum X extent; the next two are the minimum and maximum Y extent; and the final two are the minimum and maximum Z extent. The numbers are inclusive, so values of -10, 10, -10, 10, -10, 10 indicate that the dimensions of the output will be 21 x 21 x 21.
WholeExtent.label: Whole Extent

sources/SphereSource.long: Create a 3D sphere given a center and radius.
sources/SphereSource.description: The Sphere source can be used to add a polygonal sphere to the 3D scene. The output of the Sphere source is polygonal data with point normals defined.

Center.description: This property specifies the 3D coordinates for the center of the sphere.
Center.label: Center

EndPhi.description: The value of this property can be adjusted to form only a portion of a sphere. The value is measured in degrees.
EndPhi.label: End Phi

EndTheta.description: The value of this property can be adjusted to form only a portion of a sphere. This value is measured in degrees.
EndTheta.label: End Theta

PhiResolution.description: The value of this property represents the number of divisions between Start Phi and End Phi on the sphere. (See the Start Phi and End Phi properties.) The phi divisions are similar to latitude lines on the earth.
PhiResolution.label: Phi Resolution

Radius.description: This property specifies the radius of the sphere.
Radius.label: Radius

StartPhi.description: To form a complete sphere, the value of this property should be 0 degrees, and the value of the End Phi property should be 180 degrees. The value of this property can be adjusted to form only a portion of a sphere. Set the starting angle (in degrees) in the latitudinal direction.
StartPhi.label: Start Phi

StartTheta.description: To form a complete sphere, the value of this property should be 0 degrees, and the value of the End Theta property should be 360 degrees. The value of this property can be adjusted to form only a portion of a sphere.
StartTheta.label: Start Theta

ThetaResolution.description: The value of this property represents the number of divisions between Start Theta and End Theta around the sphere. (See the Start Theta and End Theta properties.) The theta divisions are similar to longitude lines on the earth. The higher the resolution, the closer the approximation will come to a sphere, and the more polygons there will be.
ThetaResolution.label: Theta Resolution

sources/SplineSource.description: This class tessellates parametric functions. The user must specify how many points in the parametric coordinate directions are required (i.e., the resolution), and the mode to use to generate scalars.

ParametricFunction.description: Property used to reference the parametric function as data generator.
ParametricFunction.label: Parametric Function

sources/spcthreader.short: Read files in the Spy Plot format.
sources/spcthreader.long: Reads files in the SPCTH Spy Plot file format.
sources/spcthreader.description: The Spy Plot reader loads an ASCII meta-file called the "case" file (extension .spcth). The case file lists all the binary files containing the dataset. This reader produces hierarchical datasets. This is a distributed reader.
sources/spcthreader.selection: Read files in the Spy Plot format.

CellArrayStatus.description: This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
CellArrayStatus.label: Cell Arrays

ComputeDerivedVariables.description: If this property is set to 1, the reader will convert derived variables like material density for the materials that the user has selected. For Density the user needs to have selected Material Mass and Material Volume Fraction.
ComputeDerivedVariables.label: Compute Derived Variables

DistributeFiles.description: In parallel mode, if this property is set to 1, the reader will distribute files or blocks.
DistributeFiles.label: Distribute Files

DownConvertVolumeFraction.description: If this property is set to 0, the type of the volume fraction is float; is set to 1, the type is unsigned char.
DownConvertVolumeFraction.label: Down Convert Volume Fraction

FileName.description: This property specifies the file name for the Spy Plot reader.
FileName.label: File Name

GenerateActiveBlockArray.description: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the active status of a block.
GenerateActiveBlockArray.label: Generate Active Block Array

GenerateBlockIdArray.description: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores a unique blockId for each block.
GenerateBlockIdArray.label: Generate Block Id Array

GenerateLevelArray.description: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the level of each block.
GenerateLevelArray.label: Generate Level Array

GenerateMarkers.description: If this property is set to 1, a second output will be created using the markers data stored in the file.
GenerateMarkers.label: Generate Markers

GenerateTracers.description: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the coordinates of any tracers.
GenerateTracers.label: Generate Tracers

MergeXYZComponents.description: If this property is set to 1, cell arrays named (for example) X velocity, Y velocity and Z velocity will be combined into a single vector array named velocity.
MergeXYZComponents.label: Merge XYZ Components

filters/StitchImageDataWithGhosts.description: Stitches images that are separated by one voxel, effectively generating ghost points at the new interfaces between the input images. Setting NumberOfGhosts to n stitches the images and generates n-1 layers of ghost cells. The inputs CANNOT have any cell data, or the filter will not run.

Input.description: This property specifies the input.
Input.label: Input

filters/StreakLine.short: Trace Streak lines through time in a vector field.
filters/StreakLine.long: Trace Streak lines through time in a vector field.
filters/StreakLine.description: The Particle Trace filter generates pathlines in a vector field from a collection of seed points. The vector field used is selected from the Vectors menu, so the input data set is required to have point-centered vectors. The Seed portion of the interface allows you to select whether the seed points for this integration lie in a point cloud or along a line. Depending on which is selected, the appropriate 3D widget (point or line widget) is displayed along with traditional user interface controls for positioning the point cloud or line within the data set. Instructions for using the 3D widgets and the corresponding manual controls can be found in section 7.4. This filter operates on any type of data set, provided it has point-centered vectors. The output is polygonal data containing polylines. This filter is available on the Toolbar.
filters/StreakLine.selection: Trace Streak lines through time in a vector field.

ComputeVorticity.description: Compute vorticity and angular rotation of particles as they progress
ComputeVorticity.label: Compute Vorticity

DisableResetCache.description: Prevents cache from getting reset so that new computation always start from previous results.
DisableResetCache.label: Disable Reset Cache

ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps.description: When animating particles, it is nice to inject new ones every Nth step to produce a continuous flow. Setting ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps to a non zero value will cause the particle source to reinject particles every Nth step even if it is otherwise unchanged. Note that if the particle source is also animated, this flag will be redundant as the particles will be reinjected whenever the source changes anyway.
ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps.label: Force Reinjection Every N Steps

Input.description: Specify which is the Input of the StreamTracer filter.
Input.label: Input

InterpolatorType.description: This property determines which interpolator to use for evaluating the velocity vector field. The first is faster though the second is more robust in locating cells during streamline integration.
InterpolatorType.label: Interpolator Type

MeshOverTime.description: The input mesh can either be 1) different over time, or 2) static over time, or 3) a linear transformation of the first time step over time, or 4) have the same topology over time. If a value other than Different are used, then performance can be improved significantly because certain data structures, such as locators or cell links are not rebuilt for each timestep.
MeshOverTime.label: Mesh Over Time

SelectInputVectors.description: Specify which vector array should be used for the integration through that filter.
SelectInputVectors.label: Select Input Vectors

Source.description: Specify the seed dataset. Typically, from where the vector field integration should begin. Usually a point/radius or a line with a given resolution.
Source.label: Seed Source

StaticSeeds.description: If the input seeds are not changing, then this can be set to 1 to avoid having to do a repeated grid search that would return the exact same result.
StaticSeeds.label: Static Seeds

filters/StreamTracer.short: Integrate streamlines in a vector field.
filters/StreamTracer.long: Integrate streamlines in a vector field.
filters/StreamTracer.description: The Stream Tracer filter generates streamlines in a vector field from a collection of seed points. Production of streamlines terminates if a streamline crosses the exterior boundary of the input dataset (ReasonForTermination=1). Other reasons for termination include an initialization issue (ReasonForTermination=2), computing an unexpected value (ReasonForTermination=3), reached the Maximum Streamline Length input value (ReasonForTermination=4), reached the Maximum Steps input value (ReasonForTermination=5), and velocity was lower than the Terminal Speed input value (ReasonForTermination=6). This filter operates on any type of dataset, provided it has point-centered vectors. The output is polygonal data containing polylines.
filters/StreamTracer.selection: Integrate streamlines in a vector field.

InitialIntegrationStep.description: This property specifies the initial integration step size. For non-adaptive integrators (Runge-Kutta 2 and Runge-Kutta 4), it is fixed (always equal to this initial value) throughout the integration. For an adaptive integrator (Runge-Kutta 4-5), the actual step size varies such that the numerical error is less than a specified threshold.
InitialIntegrationStep.label: Initial Step Length

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Stream Tracer filter.
Input.label: Input

IntegrationDirection.description: This property determines in which direction(s) a streamline is generated.
IntegrationDirection.label: Integration Direction

IntegrationStepUnit.description: This property specifies the unit for Minimum/Initial/Maximum integration step size. The Length unit refers to the arc length that a particle travels/advects within a single step. The Cell Length unit represents the step size as a number of cells.
IntegrationStepUnit.label: Integration Step Unit

IntegratorType.description: This property determines which integrator (with increasing accuracy) to use for creating streamlines.
IntegratorType.label: Integrator Type

InterpolatorType.description: This property determines which interpolator to use for evaluating the velocity vector field. The first is faster though the second is more robust in locating cells during streamline integration.
InterpolatorType.label: Interpolator Type

MaximumError.description: This property specifies the maximum error (for Runge-Kutta 4-5) tolerated throughout streamline integration. The Runge-Kutta 4-5 integrator tries to adjust the step size such that the estimated error is less than this threshold.
MaximumError.label: Maximum Error

MaximumIntegrationStep.description: When using the Runge-Kutta 4-5 integrator, this property specifies the maximum integration step size.
MaximumIntegrationStep.label: Maximum Step Length

MaximumNumberOfSteps.description: This property specifies the maximum number of steps, beyond which streamline integration is terminated.
MaximumNumberOfSteps.label: Maximum Steps

MaximumPropagation.description: This property specifies the maximum streamline length (i.e., physical arc length), beyond which line integration is terminated.
MaximumPropagation.label: Maximum Streamline Length

MinimumIntegrationStep.description: When using the Runge-Kutta 4-5 integrator, this property specifies the minimum integration step size.
MinimumIntegrationStep.label: Minimum Step Length

SelectInputVectors.description: This property contains the name of the vector array from which to generate streamlines.
SelectInputVectors.label: Vectors

Source.description: The value of this property determines how the seeds for the streamlines will be generated.
Source.label: Seed Type

Surface Streamlines.description: Specify whether to compute surface streamlines.
Surface Streamlines.label: Surface Streamlines

TerminalSpeed.description: This property specifies the terminal speed, below which particle advection/integration is terminated.
TerminalSpeed.label: Terminal Speed

UseLocalSeedSource.description: If true the filter considers that the whole seed source is available on all ranks. Else the filter will aggregate all seed sources from all ranks and merge their points. WARNING: do not set this value to true unless you know what you're doing.
UseLocalSeedSource.label: Use Local Seed Source

filters/GenericStreamTracer.short: Integrate streamlines in a vector field.
filters/GenericStreamTracer.long: Integrate streamlines in a vector field.
filters/GenericStreamTracer.description: The Generic Stream Tracer filter generates streamlines in a vector field from a collection of seed points. The vector field used is selected from the Vectors menu, so the input data set is required to have point-centered vectors. The Seed portion of the interface allows you to select whether the seed points for this integration lie in a point cloud or along a line. Depending on which is selected, the appropriate 3D widget (point or line widget) is displayed along with traditional user interface controls for positioning the point cloud or line within the data set. Instructions for using the 3D widgets and the corresponding manual controls can be found in section 7.4. The Max. Propagation entry box allows you to specify the maximum length of the streamlines. From the Max. Propagation menu, you can select the units to be either Time (the time a particle would travel with steady flow) or Length (in the data set's spatial coordinates). The Init. Step Len. menu and entry specify the initial step size for integration. (For non-adaptive integrators, Runge-Kutta 2 and 4, the initial step size is used throughout the integration.) The menu allows you to specify the units. Time and Length have the same meaning as for Max. Propagation. Cell Length specifies the step length as a number of cells. The Integration Direction menu determines in which direction(s) the stream trace will be generated: FORWARD, BACKWARD, or BOTH. The Integrator Type section of the interface determines which calculation to use for integration: Runge-Kutta 2, Runge-Kutta 4, or Runge-Kutta 4-5. If Runge-Kutta 4-5 is selected, controls are displayed for specifying the minimum and maximum step length and the maximum error. The controls for specifying Min. Step Len. and Max. Step Len. are the same as those for Init. Step Len. The Runge-Kutta 4-5 integrator tries to choose the step size so that the estimated error is less than the value of the Maximum Error entry. If the integration takes more than Max. Steps to complete, if the speed goes below Term. Speed, if Max. Propagation is reached, or if a boundary of the input data set is crossed, integration terminates. This filter operates on any type of data set, provided it has point-centered vectors. The output is polygonal data containing polylines.
filters/GenericStreamTracer.selection: Integrate streamlines in a vector field.

Input.description: Set the input to the Generic Stream Tracer filter.
Input.label: Input

IntegrationDirection.description: This property determines in which direction(s) a streamline is generated.
IntegrationDirection.label: Integration Direction

IntegrationStepUnit.description: Choose the unit to use for the integration step.
IntegrationStepUnit.label: Integration Step Unit

IntegratorType.description: This property determines which integrator (with increasing accuracy) to use for creating streamlines.
IntegratorType.label: Integrator Type

MaximumError.description: Set the maximum error allowed in the integration. The meaning of this value depends on the integrator chosen.
MaximumError.label: Maximum Error

MaximumNumberOfSteps.description: Specify the maximum number of steps used in the integration.
MaximumNumberOfSteps.label: Maximum Number Of Steps

SelectInputVectors.description: This property contains the name of the vector array from which to generate streamlines.
SelectInputVectors.label: Vectors

Source.description: The value of this property determines how the seeds for the streamlines will be generated.
Source.label: Seed Type

TerminalSpeed.description: If at any point the speed is below this value, the integration is terminated.
TerminalSpeed.label: Terminal Speed

filters/ArbitrarySourceStreamTracer.short: Integrate streamlines in a vector field.
filters/ArbitrarySourceStreamTracer.long: Integrate streamlines in a vector field.
filters/ArbitrarySourceStreamTracer.description: The Stream Tracer With Custom Source filter generates streamlines in a vector field from a collection of seed points. Production of streamlines terminates if a streamline crosses the exterior boundary of the input dataset (ReasonForTermination=1). Other reasons for termination include an initialization issue (ReasonForTermination=2), computing an unexpected value (ReasonForTermination=3), reached the Maximum Streamline Length input value (ReasonForTermination=4), reached the Maximum Steps input value (ReasonForTermination=5), and velocity was lower than the Terminal Speed input value (ReasonForTermination=6). This filter operates on any type of dataset, provided it has point-centered vectors. The output is polygonal data containing polylines. This filter takes a Source input that provides the seed points.
filters/ArbitrarySourceStreamTracer.selection: Integrate streamlines in a vector field.

InitialIntegrationStep.description: This property specifies the initial integration step size. For non-adaptive integrators (Runge-Kutta 2 and Runge-Kutta 4), it is fixed (always equal to this initial value) throughout the integration. For an adaptive integrator (Runge-Kutta 4-5), the actual step size varies such that the numerical error is less than a specified threshold.
InitialIntegrationStep.label: Initial Step Length

Input.label: Input

IntegrationDirection.description: This property determines in which direction(s) a streamline is generated.

IntegrationStepUnit.description: This property specifies the unit for Minimum/Initial/Maximum integration step size. The Length unit refers to the arc length that a particle travels/advects within a single step. The Cell Length unit represents the step size as a number of cells.
IntegrationStepUnit.label: Integration Step Unit

IntegratorType.description: This property determines which integrator (with increasing accuracy) to use for creating streamlines.
IntegratorType.label: Integrator Type

InterpolatorType.description: This property determines which interpolator to use for evaluating the velocity vector field. The first is faster though the second is more robust in locating cells during streamline integration.
InterpolatorType.label: Interpolator Type

MaximumError.description: This property specifies the maximum error (for Runge-Kutta 4-5) tolerated throughout streamline integration. The Runge-Kutta 4-5 integrator tries to adjust the step size such that the estimated error is less than this threshold.
MaximumError.label: Maximum Error

MaximumPropagation.description: This property specifies the maximum streamline length (i.e., physical arc length), beyond which line integration is terminated.
MaximumPropagation.label: Maximum Streamline Length

MinimumIntegrationStep.description: When using the Runge-Kutta 4-5 integrator, this property specifies the minimum integration step size.
MinimumIntegrationStep.label: Minimum Step Length
