SelectInputVectors.label: Vectors

Source.description: This property specifies the input used to obtain the seed points.
Source.label: Seed Source

Surface Streamlines.description: Specify whether to compute surface streamlines.
Surface Streamlines.label: Surface Streamlines

TerminalSpeed.description: This property specifies the terminal speed, below which particle advection/integration is terminated.
TerminalSpeed.label: Terminal Speed

UseLocalSeedSource.description: If true the filter considers that the whole seed source is available on all ranks. Else the filter will aggregate all seed sources from all ranks and merge their points. WARNING: do not set this value to true unless you know what you're doing.
UseLocalSeedSource.label: Use Local Seed Source

filters/Subdivide.short: Creates a surface with more triangles than the input.
filters/Subdivide.long: This filter iteratively divide triangles into four smaller triangles.  New points are placed linearly so the output surface matches the input surface.
filters/Subdivide.description: The Subdivide filter iteratively divides each triangle in the input dataset into 4 new triangles. Three new points are added per triangle -- one at the midpoint of each edge. This filter operates only on polygonal data containing triangles, so run your polygonal data through the Triangulate filter first if it is not composed of triangles. The output of this filter is also polygonal.
filters/Subdivide.selection: Creates a surface with more triangles than the input.

Input.description: This parameter specifies the input to the Subdivide filter.
Input.label: Input

NumberOfSubdivisions.description: The value of this property specifies the number of subdivision iterations to perform.
NumberOfSubdivisions.label: Number of Subdivisions

sources/SuperquadricSource.short: Create a superquadric according to the theta and phi roundness parameters
sources/SuperquadricSource.long: Create a superquadric according to the theta and phi roundness parameters. This one source can generate a wide variety of 3D objects including a box, a sphere, or a torus.
sources/SuperquadricSource.description: The Superquadric source can be used to add a polygonal superquadric to the 3D scene. This source can be used to create a wide variety of shapes (e.g., a sphere, a box, or a torus) by adjusting the roundness parameters. The output of the Superquadric source is polygonal data with point normals and texture coordinates defined.
sources/SuperquadricSource.selection: Create a superquadric according to the theta and phi roundness parameters

Center.description: This property specifies the 3D coordinates of the center of the superquadric.
Center.label: Center

PhiResolution.description: The value of this property represents the number of divisions in the phi (latitudinal) direction. This number will be rounded to the nearest multiple of 4.
PhiResolution.label: Phi Resolution

PhiRoundness.description: This property defines the roundness in the phi (latitudinal) direction. A value of 0 represents a rectangular shape, a value of 1 represents a circular shape, and values greater than 1 produce higher order shapes.
PhiRoundness.label: Phi Roundness

Scale.description: The three values in this property are used to scale the superquadric in X, Y, and Z. The surface normals will be computed correctly even with anisotropic scaling.
Scale.label: Scale

Size.description: The value of this property represents the isotropic size of the superquadric. Note that both the Size and Thickness properties control coefficients of superquadric generation, so the value of this property may not exactly describe the size of the superquadric.
Size.label: Size

ThetaResolution.description: The value of this property represents the number of divisions in the theta (longitudinal) direction. This value will be rounded to the nearest multiple of 8.
ThetaResolution.label: Theta Resolution

ThetaRoundness.description: This property defines the roundness of the superquadric in the theta (longitudinal) direction. A value of 0 represents a rectangular shape, a value of 1 represents a circular shape, and values greater than 1 produce higher order shapes.
ThetaRoundness.label: Theta Roundness

Thickness.description: If the value of the Toroidal property is 1, this value represents the thickness of the superquadric as a value between 0 and 1. A value close to 0 leads to a thin object with a large hole, and a value near 1 leads to a thick object with a very small hole. Changing the thickness does not change the outer radius of the superquadric.
Thickness.label: Thickness

Toroidal.description: If the value of this property is 0, the generated superquadric will not contain a hole (i.e., the superquadric will be ellipsoidal). Otherwise, a toroidal object is generated.
Toroidal.label: Toroidal

filters/IntegrateFlowThroughSurface.short: This filter integrates flow through a surface.
filters/IntegrateFlowThroughSurface.long: This filter integrates flow through a surface.
filters/IntegrateFlowThroughSurface.description: The flow integration filter integrates the dot product of a point flow vector field and surface normal. It computes the net flow across the 2D surface. It operates on any type of dataset and produces an unstructured grid output.
filters/IntegrateFlowThroughSurface.selection: This filter integrates flow through a surface.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Surface Flow filter.
Input.label: Input

SelectInputVectors.description: The value of this property specifies the name of the input vector array containing the flow vector field.
SelectInputVectors.label: Select Input Vectors

filters/SurfaceNormals.long: This filter will produce surface normals used for smooth shading. Splitting is used to avoid smoothing across feature edges.
filters/SurfaceNormals.description: This filter generates surface normals at the points of the input polygonal dataset to provide smooth shading of the dataset. The resulting dataset is also polygonal. The filter works by calculating a normal vector for each polygon in the dataset and then averaging the normals at the shared points.

ComputeCellNormals.description: This filter computes the normals at the points in the data set. In the process of doing this it computes polygon normals too. If you want these normals to be passed to the output of this filter, set the value of this property to 1.
ComputeCellNormals.label: Compute Cell Normals

Consistency.description: The value of this property controls whether consistent polygon ordering is enforced. Generally the normals for a data set should either all point inward or all point outward. If the value of this property is 1, then this filter will reorder the points of cells that whose normal vectors are oriented the opposite direction from the rest of those in the data set.
Consistency.label: Consistency

FeatureAngle.description: The value of this property defines a feature edge. If the surface normal between two adjacent triangles is at least as large as this Feature Angle, a feature edge exists. If Splitting is on, points are duplicated along these feature edges. (See the Splitting property.)
FeatureAngle.label: Feature Angle

FlipNormals.description: If the value of this property is 1, this filter will reverse the normal direction (and reorder the points accordingly) for all polygons in the data set; this changes front-facing polygons to back-facing ones, and vice versa. You might want to do this if your viewing position will be inside the data set instead of outside of it.
FlipNormals.label: Flip Normals

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Normals Generation filter.
Input.label: Input

NonManifoldTraversal.description: Turn on/off traversal across non-manifold edges. Not traversing non-manifold edges will prevent problems where the consistency of polygonal ordering is corrupted due to topological loops.
NonManifoldTraversal.label: Non-Manifold Traversal

PieceInvariant.description: Turn this option to to produce the same results regardless of the number of processors used (i.e., avoid seams along processor boundaries). Turn this off if you do want to process ghost levels and do not mind seams.
PieceInvariant.label: Piece Invariant

Splitting.description: This property controls the splitting of sharp edges. If sharp edges are split (property value = 1), then points are duplicated along these edges, and separate normals are computed for both sets of points to give crisp (rendered) surface definition.
Splitting.label: Splitting

filters/SurfaceTangents.long: This filter will produce surface tangents used for normal mapping.
filters/SurfaceTangents.description: This filter generates surface tangents at the points of the input polygonal dataset based on the normals and the texture coordinates. The resulting dataset is also polygonal. The tangents are required when using a normal texture.

ComputeCellTangents.description: This filter computes the tangents at the points in the data set. In the process of doing this it computes polygon tangents too. If you want these normals to be passed to the output of this filter, set the value of this property to 1.
ComputeCellTangents.label: Compute Cell Tangents

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Tangents Generation filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/SurfaceVectors.short: This filter constrains vectors to lie on a surface.
filters/SurfaceVectors.long: This filter constrains vectors to lie on a surface.
filters/SurfaceVectors.description: The Surface Vectors filter is used for 2D data sets. It constrains vectors to lie in a surface by removing components of the vectors normal to the local surface.
filters/SurfaceVectors.selection: This filter constrains vectors to lie on a surface.

ConstraintMode.description: This property specifies whether the vectors will be parallel or perpendicular to the surface. If the value is set to PerpendicularScale (2), then the output will contain a scalar array with the dot product of the surface normal and the vector at each point.
ConstraintMode.label: Constraint Mode

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Surface Vectors filter.
Input.label: Input

SelectInputVectors.description: This property specifies the name of the input vector array to process.
SelectInputVectors.label: Select Input Vectors

filters/SynchronizeTime.short: Set 'close' time step values from the source to the input
filters/SynchronizeTime.description: Synchronize time step values in the first input (Input) to time step values in the second input (Source) that are considered close enough. The outputted dataset is from the first input and the number of output time steps is also equal to the number of time steps in the first input. Time step values in the first input that are "close" to time step values in the second input are replaced with the value from the second input. Close is determined to be if the difference is less than RelativeTolerance multiplied by the time range of the first input.
filters/SynchronizeTime.selection: Set 'close' time step values from the source to the input

DataToPass.description: This property specifies the dataset whose geometry and fields will be output.
DataToPass.label: Data To Pass

TimeToSync.description: This property specifies the dataset from which to obtain the time step values.
TimeToSync.label: Time To Sync

sources/TIFFReader.long: Reads a TIFF file into an image data.
sources/TIFFReader.description: The TIFF reader reads TIFF (Tagged Image File Format) files, and the output is a uniform rectilinear (image/volume) dataset. The default file extension is .tiff.

FileName.description: This property specifies the file name for the TIFF reader.
FileName.label: File Name

sources/TIFFSeriesReader.short: Read a series of TIFF files.
sources/TIFFSeriesReader.long: Reads a series of TIFF files into an time sequence of image datas.
sources/TIFFSeriesReader.description: The TIFF series reader reads TIFF files. The output is a time sequence of uniform rectilinear (image/volume) dataset. The default file extension is .tif or .tiff.
sources/TIFFSeriesReader.selection: Read a series of TIFF files.

FileNames.description: The list of files to be read by the reader. If more than one file is specified, the reader will switch to file series mode in which it will pretend that it can support time and provide one file per time step.
FileNames.label: File Names

ReadAsImageStack.description: When set, the reader will read the set of files as an image stack, rather than a temporal file series.
ReadAsImageStack.label: Read As Image Stack

CustomDataSpacing.description: Set the spacing to use for the image output by this reader. This is used only when **UseCustomDataSpacing** is set to true.
CustomDataSpacing.label: Custom Data Spacing

UseCustomDataSpacing.description: To manually specify a custom spacing using **CustomDataSpacing**, set this property to 1 (checked).
UseCustomDataSpacing.label: Use Custom Data Spacing

sources/TruchasReader.description: Reads TRUCHAS simulation output stored in HDF5.

BlockArrayStatus.description: Select the grids to be loaded from the dataset, if any.
BlockArrayStatus.label: Blocks

CellArrayStatus.description: This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
CellArrayStatus.label: Cell Arrays

FileName.description: This property specifies the HDF5 file name
FileName.label: File Name

PointArrayStatus.description: This property lists which point-centered arrays to read.
PointArrayStatus.label: Point Arrays

filters/TableFFT.description: Performs the Fast Fourier Transform on the columns of a table.
filters/TableFFT.selection: Performs the Fast Fourier Transform on the columns of a table.

BlockOverlap.description: Specify the number of samples which will overlap between each block / segment. If value is not in a valid range (ie inferior to 0 or superior to BlockSize) then the value BlockSize / 2 will be used. Only used if UseWelchMethod is true.
BlockOverlap.label: Block Overlap

BlockSize.description: Specify the number of samples to use for each block / segment in the Welch method. This should be a power of 2 in order to achieve better performance.
BlockSize.label: Block Size

CreateFrequencyColumn.description: Specify if the filter should create a frequency column based on a column named "time" (not case sensitive). An evenly-spaced time array is expected.
CreateFrequencyColumn.label: Create Frequency Column

DefaultSampleRate.description: If the "Time" column is not found then this value will be used as the sample rate of the input.
DefaultSampleRate.label: Default Sample Rate

Detrend.description: Remove trend on each segment before applying the FFT. This is a constant detrend where the mean of the signal is substracted to the signal. Only used if UseWelchMethod is true.
Detrend.label: Detrend

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the filter.
Input.label: Input

Normalize.description: Specify if the output should be normalized. Only used if UseWelchMethod is false.
Normalize.label: Normalize

OneSidedSpectrum.description: Specify if the filter should use the optimized discrete fourier transform for real values. This will cause output columns to have from n to ((n / 2) + 1) rows.
OneSidedSpectrum.label: One Sided Spectrum

ScalingMethod.description: Set what scaling should be used when applying the Welch method.
ScalingMethod.label: Scaling Method

UseWelchMethod.description: Specify if filter should use the Welch / periodogram method. If true the input will be split in multiple segment to compute an average fft across all segments / blocks. This can be faster for input with lots of samples and also remove some noise.
UseWelchMethod.label: Use Welch Method

WindowingFunction.description: Specify the windowing function to apply on the input. This allows to better process data that is not periodic. When Welch method is used, the window is applied to each frame.
WindowingFunction.label: Windowing Function

filters/TableToPolyData.short: Converts table to set of points.
filters/TableToPolyData.long: Converts table to set of points.
filters/TableToPolyData.description: The TableToPolyData filter converts a vtkTable to a set of points in a vtkPolyData. One must specifies the columns in the input table to use as the X, Y and Z coordinates for the points in the output.
filters/TableToPolyData.selection: Converts table to set of points.

Create2DPoints.description: Specify whether the points of the polydata are 3D or 2D. If this is set to true then the Z Column will be ignored and the Z value of each point on the polydata will be set to 0. By default this will be off.
Create2DPoints.label: 2D Points

Input.description: This property specifies the input.
Input.label: Input

KeepAllDataArrays.description: Keep columns specified as X,Y,Z as Data arrays. By default this will be off.
KeepAllDataArrays.label: Keep All Data Arrays

XColumn.description: This property specifies which data array is going to be used as the X coordinate in the generated polydata dataset.
XColumn.label: X Column

YColumn.description: This property specifies which data array is going to be used as the Y coordinate in the generated polydata dataset.
YColumn.label: Y Column

ZColumn.description: This property specifies which data array is going to be used as the Z coordinate in the generated polydata dataset.
ZColumn.label: Z Column

filters/TableToStructuredGrid.short: Converts to table to structured grid.
filters/TableToStructuredGrid.long: Converts to table to structured grid.
filters/TableToStructuredGrid.description: The TableToStructuredGrid filter converts a vtkTable to a vtkStructuredGrid. One must specifies the columns in the input table to use as the X, Y and Z coordinates for the points in the output, and the whole extent.
filters/TableToStructuredGrid.selection: Converts to table to structured grid.

Input.description: This property specifies the input.
Input.label: Input

XColumn.description: This property specifies which data array is going to be used as the X coordinate in the generated polydata dataset.
XColumn.label: X Column

YColumn.description: This property specifies which data array is going to be used as the Y coordinate in the generated polydata dataset.
YColumn.label: Y Column

ZColumn.description: This property specifies which data array is going to be used as the Z coordinate in the generated polydata dataset.
ZColumn.label: Z Column

sources/TecplotReader.short: Read files in the Tecplot ASCII file format.
sources/TecplotReader.long: Reads files in the Tecplot ASCII file format.
sources/TecplotReader.description: The Tecplot reader extracts multiple zones (blocks) of data from a Tecplot ASCII file, in which a zone is stored in either point packing mode (i.e., tuple-based, with only point data supported) or block packing mode (i.e., component-based, with point data and cell data supported). The output of the reader is a vtkMultiBlockDataset, of which each block is either a vtkStructuredGrid or a vtkUnstructuredGrid. This supports reading a file series.
sources/TecplotReader.selection: Read files in the Tecplot ASCII file format.

FileNames.description: The list of files to be read by the reader.
FileNames.label: File Names

DataArrayStatus.description: This property lists what dataset attribute arrays (point data and cell data) to read.
DataArrayStatus.label: Data Arrays

sources/TecplotTableReaderCore.description: The Tecplot table reader reads a .DAT file containing tabular data into a spreadsheet view.
sources/TecplotTableReaderCore.selection: The Tecplot table reader reads a .DAT file containing tabular data into a spreadsheet view.

FileName.description: The name of the file to read.
FileName.label: File Name

Line with column names.description: The line that contains the column names.
Line with column names.label: Line with column names

Max. Number of Records.description: The maximum number of records to read. Use this to preview a file.
Max. Number of Records.label: Max. Number of Records

Number of header lines.description: The number of lines that form the header.
Number of header lines.label: Number of header lines

Skip #column name fields.description: Number of fields to skip while reading column names.
Skip #column name fields.label: Skip #column name fields

filters/TemporalArrayOperator.description: Filter used to perform an operation on a data array at 2 different timesteps.
filters/TemporalArrayOperator.selection: Filter used to perform an operation on a data array at 2 different timesteps.

FirstTimeStepIndex.description: This property specifies the timestep index to use in the first part of the comparison computation
FirstTimeStepIndex.label: First Time Step Index

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the TemporalArrayOperator filter.
Input.label: Input

Operator.description: The property determines the operation to compute between the first and second timestep data.
Operator.label: Operator

OutputArrayNameSuffix.description: This property set the suffix to be append to the output array name. If empty, output will be suffixed with '_' and the operation type.
OutputArrayNameSuffix.label: Output Array Name Suffix

SecondTimeStepIndex.description: This property specifies the timestep index to use in the second part of the comparison computation
SecondTimeStepIndex.label: Second Time Step Index

SelectInputArray.description: This property lists the name of the array from which to use.
SelectInputArray.label: Select Input Array

filters/TemporalCache.long: Saves a copy of the data set for a fixed number of time steps.
filters/TemporalCache.description: The Temporal Cache can be used to save multiple copies of a data set at different time steps to prevent thrashing in the pipeline caused by downstream filters that adjust the requested time step. For example, assume that there is a downstream Temporal Interpolator filter. This filter will (usually) request two time steps from the upstream filters, which in turn (usually) causes the upstream filters to run twice, once for each time step. The next time the interpolator requests the same two time steps, they might force the upstream filters to re-evaluate the same two time steps. The Temporal Cache can keep copies of both of these time steps and provide the requested data without having to run upstream filters.

CacheSize.description: The cache size determines the number of time steps that can be cached at one time. The maximum number is 10. The minimum is 2 (since it makes little sense to cache less than that).
CacheSize.label: Cache Size

Input.description: This property specifies the input of the Temporal Cache filter.
Input.label: Input

sources/TemporalCache.long: Saves a copy of the data set for a fixed number of time steps.
sources/TemporalCache.description: The Temporal Cache can be used to save multiple copies of a data set at different time steps to prevent thrashing in the pipeline caused by downstream filters that adjust the requested time step. For example, assume that there is a downstream Temporal Interpolator filter. This filter will (usually) request two time steps from the upstream filters, which in turn (usually) causes the upstream filters to run twice, once for each time step. The next time the interpolator requests the same two time steps, they might force the upstream filters to re-evaluate the same two time steps. The Temporal Cache can keep copies of both of these time steps and provide the requested data without having to run upstream filters.

CacheSize.description: The cache size determines the number of time steps that can be cached at one time. The maximum number is 10. The minimum is 2 (since it makes little sense to cache less than that).
CacheSize.label: Cache Size

Input.description: This property specifies the input of the Temporal Cache filter.
Input.label: Input

IsASource.description: Sets up the Algorithm to act as a pipeline source rather than a filter. This is used in Catalyst.
IsASource.label: Is A Source

filters/TemporalInterpolator.description: The Temporal Interpolator converts data that is defined at discrete time steps to one that is defined over a continuum of time by linearly interpolating the data's field data between two adjacent time steps. The interpolated values are a simple approximation and should not be interpreted as anything more. The Temporal Interpolator assumes that the topology between adjacent time steps does not change.

DiscreteTimeStepInterval.description: If Discrete Time Step Interval is set to 0, then the Temporal Interpolator will provide a continuous region of time on its output. If set to anything else, then the output will define a finite set of time points on its output, each spaced by the Discrete Time Step Interval. The output will have (time range)/(discrete time step interval) time steps. (Note that the time range is defined by the time range of the data of the input filter, which may be different from other pipeline objects or the range defined in the animation inspector.) This is a useful option to use if you have a dataset with one missing time step and wish to 'fill in' the missing data with an interpolated value from the steps on either side.
DiscreteTimeStepInterval.label: Discrete Time Step Interval

Input.description: This property specifies the input of the Temporal Interpolator.
Input.label: Input

ResampleFactor.description: When ResampleFactor is a non zero positive integer, each pair of input time steps will be interpolated between with the number of steps specified. For example an input of 1,2,3,4,5 and a resample factor of 10, will produce steps 0f 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, ..., 1.9, 2.0. Irregular input steps will produce irregular output steps. Resample factor will only be used if DiscreteTimeStepInterval is zero, otherwise the DiscreteTimeStepInterval takes precedence
ResampleFactor.label: Resample Factor

filters/ParticlePathLines.long: Creates polylines representing pathlines of animating particles
filters/ParticlePathLines.description: Particle Pathlines takes any dataset as input, it extracts the point locations of all cells over time to build up a polyline trail. The point number (index) is used as the 'key' if the points are randomly changing their respective order in the points list, then you should specify a scalar that represents the unique ID. This is intended to handle the output of a filter such as the TemporalStreamTracer.

BackwardTime.description: Compute particle path lines when time goes backward.
BackwardTime.label: Backward Time

IdChannelArray.description: Specify the name of a scalar array which will be used to fetch the index of each point. This is necessary only if the particles change position (Id order) on each time step. The Id can be used to identify particles at each step and hence track them properly. If this array is set to "Global or Local IDs", the global point ids are used if they exist or the point index is otherwise.
IdChannelArray.label: Id Channel Array

Input.description: The input cells for which to create pathlines.
Input.label: Input

KeepDeadTrails.description: Keep the trails of particles that leave the domain. Use carefully as it may cause excessive memory consumption when generating many particle trails.
KeepDeadTrails.label: Keep Dead Trails

MaskPoints.description: Set the number of particles to track as a ratio of the input. Example: setting MaskPoints to 10 will track every 10th point.
MaskPoints.label: Mask Points

MaxStepDistance.description: If a particle disappears from one end of a simulation and reappears on the other side, the track left will be unrepresentative. Set a MaxStepDistance{x,y,z} which acts as a threshold above which if a step occurs larger than the value (for the dimension), the track will be dropped and restarted after the step. That is, the part before the wrap around will be dropped and the newer part kept.
MaxStepDistance.label: Max Step Distance

MaxTrackLength.description: If the particles being traced animate for a long time, the trails or traces will become long and stringy. Setting the MaxTraceTimeLength will limit how much of the trace is displayed. Tracks longer then the Max will disappear and the trace will appear like a snake of fixed length which progresses as the particle moves. This length is given with respect to timesteps.
MaxTrackLength.label: Max Track Length

Selection.description: Set a second input, which is a selection. Particles with the same Id in the selection as the primary input will be chosen for pathlines. Note that you must have the same IdChannelArray in the selection as the input.
Selection.label: Selection

filters/TemporalShiftScale.description: The Temporal Shift Scale filter linearly transforms the time values of a pipeline object by applying a shift and then scale. Given a data at time t on the input, it will be transformed to time t*Shift + Scale on the output. Inversely, if this filter has a request for time t, it will request time (t-Shift)/Scale on its input.

Input.description: The input to the Temporal Shift Scale filter.
Input.label: Input

MaximumNumberOfPeriods.description: If Periodic time is enabled, this controls how many time periods time is reported for. A filter cannot output an infinite number of time steps and therefore a finite number of periods is generated when reporting time.
MaximumNumberOfPeriods.label: Maximum Number Of Periods

Periodic.description: If Periodic is true, requests for time will be wrapped around so that the source appears to be a periodic time source. If data exists for times {0,N-1}, setting periodic to true will cause time 0 to be produced when time N, 2N, 2N etc is requested. This effectively gives the source the ability to generate time data indefinitely in a loop. When combined with Shift/Scale, the time becomes periodic in the shifted and scaled time frame of reference. Note: Since the input time may not start at zero, the wrapping of time from the end of one period to the start of the next, will subtract the initial time - a source with T{5..6} repeated periodically will have output time {5..6..7..8} etc.
Periodic.label: Periodic

PeriodicEndCorrection.description: If Periodic time is enabled, this flag determines if the last time step is the same as the first. If PeriodicEndCorrection is true, then it is assumed that the input data goes from 0-1 (or whatever scaled/shifted actual time) and time 1 is the same as time 0 so that steps will be 0,1,2,3...N,1,2,3...N,1,2,3 where step N is the same as 0 and step 0 is not repeated. When this flag is false the data is assumed to be literal and output is of the form 0,1,2,3...N,0,1,2,3... By default this flag is ON
PeriodicEndCorrection.label: Periodic End Correction

PostShift.description: The amount of time the input is shifted.
PostShift.label: Post Shift

PreShift.description: Apply a translation to the data before scaling. To convert T{5,100} to T{0,1} use Preshift=-5, Scale=1/95, PostShift=0 To convert T{5,105} to T{5,10} use Preshift=-5, Scale=5/100, PostShift=5
PreShift.label: Pre Shift

Scale.description: The factor by which the input time is scaled.
Scale.label: Scale

filters/TemporalSmoothing.short: Smooths a temporal input over a sliding temporal window.
filters/TemporalSmoothing.long: This filter smooths a temporal input's point and cell data by computing an average over a temporal window.
filters/TemporalSmoothing.description: Given an input that changes over time, Temporal Smoothing will provide an average of each point and cell data values over a temporal window centered on a requested time step. Because of this, the input's topology is assumed to not change over time, and so the number and order of its points and cells should stay the same. In order to provide comparable results for different time steps, the temporal window must be the same size. To enforce this the filter clips its input available time steps to allow the full window size to fit. If an out-of-bound time step is requested, the filter will use the closest available time step. Note that updating this filter will trigger upstream updates for each time steps of the window, which could be expensive.
filters/TemporalSmoothing.selection: Smooths a temporal input over a sliding temporal window.

Input.description: Set the input to the Temporal Smoothing filter.
Input.label: Input

TemporalWindowHalfWidth.description: Set the temporal window half width. When requesting a time step, the associated data will be smoothed using this number of time steps before and after it. The resulting window's width is (halfwidth*2)+1 time steps. This property also influences the number of timesteps produced by the filter to exclude time steps where the full window cannot be applied.
TemporalWindowHalfWidth.label: Temporal Window Half Width

filters/TemporalSnapToTimeStep.short: Modifies the time range/steps of temporal data.
filters/TemporalSnapToTimeStep.long: Modifies the time range/steps of temporal data.
filters/TemporalSnapToTimeStep.description: This file modifies the time range or time steps of the data without changing the data itself. The data is not resampled by this filter, only the information accompanying the data is modified.
filters/TemporalSnapToTimeStep.selection: Modifies the time range/steps of temporal data.

Input.description: This property specifies the input of the filter.
Input.label: Input

SnapMode.description: Determine which time step to snap to.
SnapMode.label: Snap Mode

filters/TemporalStatistics.long: Loads in all time steps of a dataset and computes some statistics about how each point and cell variable changes over time.
filters/TemporalStatistics.description: Given an input that changes over time, Temporal Statistics looks at the data for each time step and computes some statistical information of how a point or cell variable changes over time. For example, Temporal Statistics can compute the average value of "pressure" over time of each point. Note that this filter will require the upstream filter to be run on every time step that it reports that it can compute. This may be a time consuming operation. Temporal Statistics ignores the temporal spacing. Each timestep will be weighted the same regardless of how long of an interval it is to the next timestep. Thus, the average statistic may be quite different from an integration of the variable if the time spacing varies.

ComputeAverage.description: Compute the average of each point and cell variable over time.
ComputeAverage.label: Compute Average

ComputeMaximum.description: Compute the maximum of each point and cell variable over time.
ComputeMaximum.label: Compute Maximum

ComputeMinimum.description: Compute the minimum of each point and cell variable over time.
ComputeMinimum.label: Compute Minimum

ComputeStandardDeviation.description: Compute the standard deviation of each point and cell variable over time.
ComputeStandardDeviation.label: Compute Standard Deviation

Input.description: Set the input to the Temporal Statistics filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/TensorGlyph.short: This filter generates an ellipsoid, cuboid, cylinder or superquadric glyph at each        point of the input data set. The glyphs are oriented and scaled according to eigenvalues        and eigenvectors of tensor point data of the input data set.        This filter supports symmetric tensors. Symmetric tensor components are expected to have        the following order: XX, YY, ZZ, XY, YZ, XZ
filters/TensorGlyph.long: This filter generates an ellipsoid, cuboid, cylinder or superquadric glyph at        each point of the input data set. The glyphs are oriented and scaled according        to eigenvalues and eigenvectors of tensor point data of the input data set.        This filter supports symmetric tensors. Symmetric tensor are expected to have        the following order: XX, YY, ZZ, XY, YZ, XZ
filters/TensorGlyph.description: The Tensor Glyph filter generates an ellipsoid, cuboid, cylinder or superquadric glyph at every point in the input data set. The glyphs are oriented and scaled according to eigenvalues and eigenvectors of tensor point data of the input data set. The Tensor Glyph filter operates on any type of data set. Its output is polygonal. This filter supports symmetric tensors. Symmetric tensor components are expected to have the following order: XX, YY, ZZ, XY, YZ, XZ"
filters/TensorGlyph.selection: This filter generates an ellipsoid, cuboid, cylinder or superquadric glyph at each        point of the input data set. The glyphs are oriented and scaled according to eigenvalues        and eigenvectors of tensor point data of the input data set.        This filter supports symmetric tensors. Symmetric tensor components are expected to have        the following order: XX, YY, ZZ, XY, YZ, XZ

ColorGlyphs.description: This property determines whether or not to color the glyphs.
ColorGlyphs.label: Color Glyphs

ColorMode.description: This property determines whether input scalars or computed eigenvalues at the point should be used to color the glyphs. If ThreeGlyphs is set and the eigenvalues are chosen for coloring then each glyph is colored by the corresponding eigenvalue and if not set the color corresponding to the largest eigenvalue is chosen.
ColorMode.label: Color by

ExtractEigenvalues.description: Toggle whether to extract eigenvalues from tensor. If false, eigenvalues/eigenvectors are not extracted and the columns of the tensor are taken as the eigenvectors (the norm of column, always positive, is the eigenvalue). If true, the glyph is scaled and oriented according to eigenvalues and eigenvectors; additionally, eigenvalues are provided as new data array.
ExtractEigenvalues.label: Extract Eigenvalues

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Glyph filter.
Input.label: Input

LimitScalingByEigenvalues.description: This property determines whether scaling of glyphs by ScaleFactor times eigenvalue should be limited. This is useful to prevent uncontrolled scaling near singularities.
LimitScalingByEigenvalues.label: Limit Scaling By Eigenvalues

MaxScaleFactor.description: If scaling by eigenvalues should be limited, this value sets an upper limit for scale factor times eigenvalue.
MaxScaleFactor.label: Max Scale Factor

ScaleFactor.description: This property specifies the scale factor to scale every glyph by.
ScaleFactor.label: Scale Factor

SelectInputScalars.description: This property indicates the name of the scalar array to use for coloring
SelectInputScalars.label: Scalars

SelectInputTensors.description: This property indicates the name of the tensor array on which to operate. The indicated array's eigenvalues and eigenvectors are used for scaling and orienting the glyphs.
SelectInputTensors.label: Tensors

Source.description: This property determines which type of glyph will be placed at the points in the input dataset.
Source.label: Glyph Type

Symmetric.description: This property determines whether or not to draw a mirror of each glyph.
Symmetric.label: Symmetric

ThreeGlyphs.description: Toggle whether to produce three glyphs, each of which oriented along an eigenvector and scaled according to the corresponding eigenvector.
ThreeGlyphs.label: Three Glyphs

filters/TensorPrincipalInvariants.short: Computes tensor principal values and directions.
filters/TensorPrincipalInvariants.long: Computes principal values and directions from 2D and 3D tensors.
filters/TensorPrincipalInvariants.description: This filter computes principal values and directions for 2D and 3D tensors. The principal vectors can be scaled by their corresponding principal values.
filters/TensorPrincipalInvariants.selection: Computes tensor principal values and directions.

CellTensors.description: Cell tensors from which to compute principal invariants.
CellTensors.label: Cell Tensors

Input.description: This property specifies the input.
Input.label: Input

PointTensors.description: Point tensors from which to compute principal invariants.
PointTensors.label: Point Tensors

ScalePrincipalVectorsWithPrincipalValues.description: Principal vectors can be scaled by the principal values instead of being unitary.
ScalePrincipalVectorsWithPrincipalValues.label: Scale Principal Vectors With Principal Values

filters/TessellatorFilter.long: Tessellate nonlinear curves, surfaces, and volumes with lines, triangles, and tetrahedra.
filters/TessellatorFilter.description: The Tessellate filter tessellates cells with nonlinear geometry and/or scalar fields into a simplicial complex with linearly interpolated field values that more closely approximate the original field. This is useful for datasets containing quadratic cells.

ChordError.description: This property controls the maximum chord error allowed at any edge midpoint in the output tessellation. The chord error is measured as the distance between the midpoint of any output edge and the original nonlinear geometry.
ChordError.label: Chord Error

FieldError2.description: This property controls the maximum field error allowed at any edge midpoint in the output tessellation. The field error is measured as the difference between a field value at the midpoint of an output edge and the value of the corresponding field in the original nonlinear geometry.
FieldError2.label: Field Error

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Tessellate filter.
Input.label: Input

MaximumNumberOfSubdivisions.description: This property specifies the maximum number of times an edge may be subdivided. Increasing this number allows further refinement but can drastically increase the computational and storage requirements, especially when the value of the OutputDimension property is 3.
MaximumNumberOfSubdivisions.label: Maximum Number of Subdivisions

MergePoints.description: If the value of this property is set to 1, coincident vertices will be merged after tessellation has occurred. Only geometry is considered during the merge and the first vertex encountered is the one whose point attributes will be used. Any discontinuities in point fields will be lost. On the other hand, many operations, such as streamline generation, require coincident vertices to be merged. Toggle whether to merge coincident vertices.
MergePoints.label: Merge Points

OutputDimension.description: The value of this property sets the maximum dimensionality of the output tessellation. When the value of this property is 3, 3D cells produce tetrahedra, 2D cells produce triangles, and 1D cells produce line segments. When the value is 2, 3D cells will have their boundaries tessellated with triangles. When the value is 1, all cells except points produce line segments.
OutputDimension.label: Output Dimension

Input.description: Set the input to the Generic Tessellator filter.
Input.label: Input

sources/Test3DWidget.selection: Native test-widget source; no production modelling or scientific-result qualification is claimed.

Resolution.description: Set the number of faces used to generate the cone.
Resolution.label: Resolution

filters/DataSetTriangleFilter.long: This filter converts 3-d cells to tetrahedrons and polygons to triangles.  The output is always of type unstructured grid.
filters/DataSetTriangleFilter.description: The Tetrahedralize filter converts the 3D cells of any type of dataset to tetrahedrons and the 2D ones to triangles. This filter always produces unstructured grid output.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Tetrahedralize filter.
Input.label: Input

sources/TextSource.long: The Text source generates a table containing text.
sources/TextSource.description: The Text source is used to generate a vtkTable with a single text string. To create a table with several columns, use the '|' (pipe) character. To create several rows, simply add newlines.

Text.description: This property specifies the text to display. To display text separated into cells, use newlines to separate text into rows and the '|' (pipe) character to create columns.
Text.label: Text

filters/TextureMapToCylinder.short: Generate texture coordinates by mapping points to cylinder.
filters/TextureMapToCylinder.long: Generate texture coordinates by mapping points to cylinder.
filters/TextureMapToCylinder.description: This is a filter that generates 2D texture coordinates by mapping input dataset points onto a cylinder. The cylinder is generated automatically. The cylinder is generated automatically by computing the axis of the cylinder. Note that the generated texture coordinates for the s-coordinate ranges from (0-1) (corresponding to angle of 0->360 around axis), while the mapping of the t-coordinate is controlled by the projection of points along the axis.
filters/TextureMapToCylinder.selection: Generate texture coordinates by mapping points to cylinder.

GenerateCylinderAutomatically.description: When set, the filter will try to determine the size and orientation of the cylinder used for texture mapping using data bounds.
GenerateCylinderAutomatically.label: Generate Cylinder Automatically

Input.description: Set the input to the Texture Map to Cylinder filter.
Input.label: Input

Point1.description: When **GenerateCylinderAutomatically** is not set, specify the first point defining the axis of the cylinder through its center.
Point1.label: Point1

Point2.description: When **GenerateCylinderAutomatically** is not set, specify the second point defining the axis of the cylinder through its center.
Point2.label: Point2

PreventSeam.description: Control how the texture coordinates are generated. If Prevent Seam is set, the s-coordinate ranges from 0->1 and 1->0 corresponding to the theta angle variation between 0->180 and 180->0 degrees. Otherwise, the s-coordinate ranges from 0->1 between 0->360 degrees.
PreventSeam.label: Prevent Seam

filters/TextureMapToPlane.short: Generate texture coordinates by mapping points to plane.
filters/TextureMapToPlane.long: Generate texture coordinates by mapping points to plane.
filters/TextureMapToPlane.description: TextureMapToPlane is a filter that generates 2D texture coordinates by mapping input dataset points onto a plane. The plane is generated automatically. A least squares method is used to generate the plane automatically.
filters/TextureMapToPlane.selection: Generate texture coordinates by mapping points to plane.

Automatic.description: If set the plane values will be automatically generated. Note that for this to work all the Origin, Point1 and Point2 must all be set to zero.
Automatic.label: Automatic

Input.description: Set the input to the Texture Map to Plane filter.
Input.label: Input

Origin.description: This property specifies the 3D coordinates for the origin of the plane. Set all to zero if you want to use automatic generation.
Origin.label: Origin

Point1.description: This property specifies the 3D coordinates for Point1 of the plane. Set all to zero if you want to use automatic generation.
Point1.label: Point1

Point2.description: This property specifies the 3D coordinates for Point2 of the plane. Set all to zero if you want to use automatic generation.
Point2.label: Point2

filters/TextureMapToSphere.short: Generate texture coordinates by mapping points to sphere.
filters/TextureMapToSphere.long: Generate texture coordinates by mapping points to sphere.
filters/TextureMapToSphere.description: This is a filter that generates 2D texture coordinates by mapping input dataset points onto a sphere. The sphere is generated automatically. The sphere is generated automatically by computing the center i.e. averaged coordinates, of the sphere. Note that the generated texture coordinates range between (0,1). The s-coordinate lies in the angular direction around the z-axis, measured counter-clockwise from the x-axis. The t-coordinate lies in the angular direction measured down from the north pole towards the south pole.
filters/TextureMapToSphere.selection: Generate texture coordinates by mapping points to sphere.

Input.description: Set the input to the Texture Map to Sphere filter.
Input.label: Input

PreventSeam.description: Control how the texture coordinates are generated. If Prevent Seam is set, the s-coordinate ranges from 0->1 and 1->0 corresponding to the theta angle variation between 0->180 and 180->0 degrees. Otherwise, the s-coordinate ranges from 0->1 between 0->360 degrees.
PreventSeam.label: Prevent Seam

filters/Threshold.short: Extract cells that satisfy a threshold criterion.
filters/Threshold.long: This filter extracts cells that have point or cell scalars in the specified range.
filters/Threshold.description: The Threshold filter extracts the portions of the input dataset whose scalars lie within the specified range. This filter operates on either point-centered or cell-centered data. It operates on any type of dataset and produces unstructured grid output. The scalar array from which to threshold the data can be selected in the 'Scalars' menu. For a multi-components array, 'Selected Component' menu allows you to select a specific component or magnitude if using the 'Selected' component mode. You can also choose 'All' or 'Any' that will keep data if either all components or at least one satisfies the threshold. Note that multi-components arrays are not available with Hyper Tree Grid inputs. The 'Lower Threshold' and 'Upper Threshold' sliders determine the range of the scalars to retain in the output. The threshold method can be selected from the 'Threshold Method' menu. The 'All Scalars' option only applies to Point Data. When this option is on, a cell will only be passed to the output if the scalar values of all of its points lie within the chosen range. When off, a cell will be added to the output if the specified scalar value for any of its points is within the chosen range.
filters/Threshold.selection: Extract cells that satisfy a threshold criterion.

AllScalars.description: If the value of this property is 1, then a cell is only included in the output if the value of the selected array for all its points is within the threshold. This is only relevant when thresholding by a point-centered array.
AllScalars.label: All Scalars

ComponentMode.description: This property specifies how multi-component arrays are handled. 'Selected' will use the 'Selected Component' property. 'All' will pass if all components satisfy the rule. 'Any' will pass if any component satisfies the rule.
ComponentMode.label: Component Mode

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Threshold filter.
Input.label: Input

Invert.description: Invert the threshold results. That is, cells that would have been in the output with this option off are excluded, while cells that would have been excluded from the output are included.
Invert.label: Invert

LowerThreshold.description: The value of this property specifies the lower bound of the thresholding operation.
LowerThreshold.label: Lower Threshold

MemoryStrategy.description: Select how to construct the result in memory: - MaskInput (default): shallow copy the input and mask all cells being thresholded - Regenerate Trees And Index Fields: generate a new tree structure but use indexed arrays on the input for cell data - New HyperTreeGrid: construct a new HyperTreeGrid from scratch representing the minimal threshold of the input
MemoryStrategy.label: Memory Strategy

SelectInputScalars.description: The value of this property contains the name of the array from which to perform thresholding. Be aware that HTG does not support multi-component arrays.
SelectInputScalars.label: Scalars

SelectedComponent.description: This property specifies which component of the array needs to satisfy the rule.
SelectedComponent.label: Selected Component

ThresholdMethod.description: This property indicates the threshold method.
ThresholdMethod.label: Threshold Method

UpperThreshold.description: The value of this property specifies the upper bound of the thresholding operation.
UpperThreshold.label: Upper Threshold

UseContinuousCellRange.description: If off, the vertex scalars are treated as a discrete set. If on, they are treated as a continuous interval over the minimum and maximum. One important "on" use case: When setting lower and upper threshold equal to some value and turning AllScalars off, the results are cells containing the isosurface for that value. WARNING: Whether on or off, for higher order input, the filter will not give accurate results.
UseContinuousCellRange.label: Use Continuous Cell Range

sources/ThresholdSelectionSource.description: ThresholdSelectionSource is used to create a threshold based selection.
sources/ThresholdSelectionSource.selection: ThresholdSelectionSource is used to create a threshold based selection.

ArrayName.description: For threshold and value selection, this controls the name of the scalar array that will be thresholded within.
ArrayName.label: Array Name

ContainingCells.description: When field type is POINT, this controls whether single vertex cells will be produced for each selected point, or whether the cells that contain each selected point will be produced. When field type is CELL this has no effect.
ContainingCells.label: Containing Cells

FieldType.description: The location of the array the selection came from (e.g. point, cell).
FieldType.label: Field Type

InsideOut.description: When this property is false the selection describes everything that should be extracted. When this is true the selection describes everything that should NOT be extracted.
InsideOut.label: Inside Out

filters/ThresholdTable.long: This filter extracts table rows that satisfy a threshold criterion for a given column.
filters/ThresholdTable.description: The Threshold Table Filter uses minimum and/or maximum values to threshold table rows based on the values in a particular column of a vtkTable object. It operates on scalar fields, and accepts two thresholding parameters: MinValue and MaxValue. This filter offers four different thresholding methods : "Below Max Threshold", "Above Min Threshold", "Between", and "Outside". The output of this filter is a vtkTable object with less or as many rows as the input vtkTable.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Threshold Table filter.
Input.label: Input

MaxValue.description: The value of this property specifies the upper bound of the thresholding operation.
MaxValue.label: Max Value

MinValue.description: The value of this property specifies the lower bound of the thresholding operation.
MinValue.label: Min Value

filters/Stripper.long: This filter uses a greedy algorithm to convert triangles into triangle strips
filters/Stripper.description: The Triangle Strips filter converts triangles into triangle strips and lines into polylines. This filter operates on polygonal data sets and produces polygonal output.

filters/TriangleFilter.long: This filter converts polygons and triangle strips to basic triangles.
filters/TriangleFilter.description: The Triangulate filter decomposes polygonal data into only triangles, points, and lines. It separates triangle strips and polylines into individual triangles and lines, respectively. The output is polygonal data. Some filters that take polygonal data as input require that the data be composed of triangles rather than other polygons, so passing your data through this filter first is useful in such situations. You should use this filter in these cases rather than the Tetrahedralize filter because they produce different output dataset types. The filters referenced require polygonal input, and the Tetrahedralize filter produces unstructured grid output.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the Triangulate filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/TubeFilter.description: The Tube filter creates tubes around the lines in the input polygonal dataset. The output is also polygonal.

NumberOfSides.description: The value of this property indicates the number of faces around the circumference of the tube.
NumberOfSides.label: Number of Sides

Radius.description: The value of this property sets the radius of the tube. If the radius is varying (VaryRadius property), then this value is the minimum radius.
Radius.label: Radius

RadiusFactor.description: If varying the radius (VaryRadius property), the property sets the maximum tube radius in terms of a multiple of the minimum radius. If not varying the radius, this value has no effect.
RadiusFactor.label: Radius Factor

SelectInputScalars.description: This property indicates the name of the scalar array on which to operate. The indicated array may be used for scaling the tubes. (See the VaryRadius property.)

If the radius varies by vector, a mass flux preserving variation is used. If it varies by absolute scalar, the radius is equal to the scalar field (which thus must be positive!). If it varies by vector norm, the vector magnitude is used in varying the radius.

filters/ValidateCells.long: vtkCellValidator accepts as input a dataset and adds integral cell data  to it corresponding to the validity of each cell. The validity field  encodes a bitfield for identifying problems that prevent a cell from standard  use, including:     WrongNumberOfPoints: filters assume that a cell has access to the                         appropriate number of points that comprise it. This                         assumption is often tacit, resulting in unexpected                         behavior when the condition is not met. This check                         simply confirms that the cell has the minimum number                         of points needed to describe it.     IntersectingEdges: cells that incorrectly describe the order of their                       points often manifest with intersecting edges or                       intersecting faces. Given a tolerance, this check                       ensures that two edges from a two-dimensional cell                       are separated by at least the tolerance (discounting                       end-to-end connections).     IntersectingFaces: cells that incorrectly describe the order of their                       points often manifest with intersecting edges or                       intersecting faces. Given a tolerance, this check                       ensures that two faces from a three-dimensional cell                       do not intersect.     NoncontiguousEdges: another symptom of incorrect point ordering within a                        cell is the presence of noncontiguous edges where                        contiguous edges are otherwise expected. Given a                        tolerance, this check ensures that edges around the                        perimeter of a two-dimensional cell are contiguous.     Nonconvex: many algorithms implicitly require that all input three-               dimensional cells be convex. This check uses the generic               convexity checkers implemented in vtkPolygon and vtkPolyhedron               to test this requirement.     FacesAreOrientedIncorrectly: All three-dimensional cells have an implicit                                 expectation for the orientation of their                                 faces. While the convention is unfortunately                                 inconsistent across cell types, it is usually                                 required that cell faces point outward. This                                 check tests that the faces of a cell point in                                 the direction required by the cell type,                                 taking into account the cell types with                                 nonstandard orientation requirements.

filters/VolumeOfRevolution.short: Create a point array representing elevation.
filters/VolumeOfRevolution.long: Create point attribute array by projecting points onto an elevation vector.
filters/VolumeOfRevolution.selection: Create a point array representing elevation.

AxisDirection.description: The direction of the axis of revolution.
AxisDirection.label: Axis Direction

AxisPosition.description: Position of the rotational axis in 3D space.
AxisPosition.label: Axis Position

Resolution.description: Sets the number of samples to create about the **Sweep Angle**. Each segment in the output is created in equal-angle segments.
Resolution.label: Resolution

SweepAngle.description: Sets the angle (in degrees) of the rotational sweep to perform. Valid range is 0 to 360.
SweepAngle.label: Sweep Angle

filters/PMergeConnected.long: Use global RegionId and merge cells with the same RegionId to a polyhedron cell

Input.description: This property specifies the input for this filter.
Input.label: Input

filters/VortexCores.short: Compute vortex cores of a vector field
filters/VortexCores.description: Compute vortex core lines using the parallel vectors method. By default, the "Higher-Order" approach of computing the parallel vector lines between the flow field's velocity and jerk is disabled in favor of computing the parallel vector lines between the velocity and acceleration. To further discriminate against spurious vortex cores, at each potential point value the Q-criterion, delta-criterion, lambda_ci, and lambda_2-criterion are checked. The Q-criterion and delta-criterion are used to prefilter cells prior to the execution of the parallel lines algorithm, and all criteria values are stored as point values on the output polylines.
filters/VortexCores.selection: Compute vortex cores of a vector field

FasterApproximation.description: When this option is enabled, the gradient filter used to compute vortex cores will provide a less accurate algorithm that performs fewer derivative calculations and is therefore faster.
FasterApproximation.label: Faster Approximation

Input.description: The input.
Input.label: Input

SelectInputArray.description: This property indicates the name of the vector array from which to compute vortex cores.
SelectInputArray.label: Vector Field

UseHigherOrderMethod.description: Use the flow field's jerk instead of acceleration as the second vector field during the parallel vector operation. Disabled by default.
UseHigherOrderMethod.label: Use Higher Order Method

filters/WarpScalar.short: Warp point scalars into a spatial elevation plot.
filters/WarpScalar.long: This filter moves point coordinates along a vector scaled by a point attribute.  It can be used to produce carpet plots.
filters/WarpScalar.description: The Warp By Scalar filter translates the points of the input dataset along a vector by a distance determined by the specified scalars. This filter operates on polygonal, curvilinear, and unstructured grid datasets containing single-component scalar arrays. Because it only changes the positions of the points, the output dataset type is the same as that of the input. Any scalars in the input dataset are copied to the output, so the data can be colored by them.
filters/WarpScalar.selection: Warp point scalars into a spatial elevation plot.

GenerateEnclosure.description: If this value is checked and the active dataset is a 2D surface, generate a water-tight enclosure containing the initial surface, the warped surface and "side walls".
GenerateEnclosure.label: Generate Enclosure

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the filter.
Input.label: Input

Normal.description: The values of this property specify the direction along which to warp the dataset if any normals contained in the input dataset are not being used for this purpose. (See the UseNormal property.)
Normal.label: Normal

ScaleFactor.description: The scalar value at a given point is multiplied by the value of this property to determine the magnitude of the change vector for that point.
ScaleFactor.label: Scale Factor

SelectInputScalars.description: This property contains the name of the scalar array by which to warp the dataset.
SelectInputScalars.label: Scalars

UseNormal.description: If point normals are present in the dataset, the value of this property toggles whether to use a single normal value (value = 1) or the normals from the dataset (value = 0).
UseNormal.label: Use Normal

XYPlane.description: If the value of this property is 1, then the Z-coordinates from the input are considered to be the scalar values, and the displacement is along the Z axis. This is useful for creating carpet plots.
XYPlane.label: XY Plane

filters/WarpVector.short: Warp (displace) the geometry with a given vector field.
filters/WarpVector.long: This filter displaces point coordinates along a vector attribute. It is useful for showing mechanical deformation.
filters/WarpVector.description: The Warp By Vector filter translates the points of the input dataset using a specified vector array. The vector array chosen specifies a vector per point in the input. Each point is translated along its vector by a given scale factor. This filter operates on polygonal, curvilinear, and unstructured grid datasets. Because this filter only changes the positions of the points, the output dataset type is the same as that of the input.
filters/WarpVector.selection: Warp (displace) the geometry with a given vector field.

Input.description: This property specifies the input to the filter.
Input.label: Input

ScaleFactor.description: Each component of the selected vector array will be multiplied by the value of this property before being used to compute new point coordinates.
ScaleFactor.label: Scale Factor

SelectInputVectors.description: The value of this property contains the name of the vector array by which to warp the dataset's point coordinates.
SelectInputVectors.label: Vectors

sources/RTAnalyticSource.short: Create a rectilinear grid containing a wavelet
sources/RTAnalyticSource.long: Create a regular rectilinear grid in up to three dimensions with values varying according to a periodic function.
sources/RTAnalyticSource.description: The Wavelet source can be used to create a uniform rectilinear grid in up to three dimensions with values varying according to the following periodic function. OS = M * exp(-r^2 / (2 * SD^2)) + XM * sin(XF * x) + YM * sin(YF * y) + ZM * cos(ZF * z). OS is the output scalar; M is the maximum value (the Gaussian amplitude) and SD the standard deviation of the Gaussian; r is the distance from the centre; XM, YM, and ZM are the X, Y, and Z magnitude values; and XF, YF, and ZF are the X, Y, and Z frequency values. The terms are added, not multiplied, and the coordinates are offsets from the centre divided by the extent width (vtkRTAnalyticSource; ParaView's own documentation writes the terms as a product, Schemaxis correction). If a two-dimensional extent is specified, the resulting image will be displayed. If a three-dimensional extent is used, then the bounding box of the volume will be displayed.
sources/RTAnalyticSource.selection: Create a rectilinear grid containing a wavelet
sources/RTAnalyticSource.basis: curated correction of installed native documentation

captured.description: The Wavelet source can be used to create a uniform rectilinear grid in up to three dimensions with values varying according to the following periodic function. OS = M * G * (XM * sin(XF * x) + YM * sin(YF * y) + ZM * cos(ZF * z)) OS is the output scalar; M represents the maximum value; G represents the Gaussian; XM, YM, and ZM are the X, Y, and Z magnitude values; and XF, YF, and ZF are the X, Y, and Z frequency values. If a two-dimensional extent is specified, the resulting image will be displayed. If a three-dimensional extent is used, then the bounding box of the volume will be displayed.

sources/WindBladeReader.long: Reads WindBlade/Firetec simulation files possibly including wind turbines and topology files.
sources/WindBladeReader.description: WindBlade/Firetec is a simulation dealing with the effects of wind on wind turbines or on the spread of fires. It produces three outputs: port 0 (Field) is a StructuredGrid for the wind data fields, port 1 (Blade) is an UnstructuredGrid for turning turbine blades and port 2 (Ground) is a StructuredGrid for the ground topology (ParaView's OutputPort order; its prose lists them in a different order and calls the blades a PolyData, but vtkWindBladeReader declares vtkUnstructuredGrid on port 1; Schemaxis correction). The input file (.wind) opened by the WindBlade reader is an ASCII description of the data files expected. Data is accumulated by the simulation processor and is written one file per time step. WindBlade can deal with topology if a flag is turned on and expects (x,y) data for the ground. It also can deal with turning wind turbines from other time step data files which gives polygon positions of segments of the blades and data for each segment. This is a distributed reader.
sources/WindBladeReader.basis: curated correction of installed native documentation

captured.description: WindBlade/Firetec is a simulation dealing with the effects of wind on wind turbines or on the spread of fires. The input file (.wind) opened by the WindBlade reader is an ASCII description of the data files expected. Data is accumulated by the simulation processor and is written one file per time step. WindBlade can deal with topology if a flag is turned on and expects (x,y) data for the ground. It also can deal with turning wind turbines from other time step data files which gives polygon positions of segments of the blades and data for each segment. This is a distributed reader.

NumberOfIORanks.description: In parallel runs, this writer can consolidate output from multiple ranks to a subset of ranks. This specifies the number of ranks that will do the final writing to disk. If **NumberOfIORanks** is 0, then all ranks will save the local data. If set to 1 (default), the root node alone will write to disk. All data from all ranks will be gathered to the root node before being written out.
NumberOfIORanks.label: Number Of IO Ranks

RankAssignmentMode.description: When **NumberOfIORanks** is greater than 1 and less than the number of MPI ranks, this controls how the ranks that write to disk are determined. This also affects which ranks send data to which rank for IO. In **Contiguous** mode (default), all MPI ranks are numerically grouped into **NumberOfIORanks** groups with the first rank in each group acting as the `root` node for that group and is the one that does IO. For example, if there are 16 MPI ranks and NumberOfIORanks is set to 3 then the groups are `[0 - 5], [6 - 10], [11 - 15]` with the first rank in each group 0, 6, and 15 doing the IO. In **RoundRobin** mode, the grouping is done in round robin fashion, thus for 16 MPI ranks with NumberOfIORanks set to 3, the groups are `[0, 3, ..., 15], [1, 4, ..., 13], [2, 5, ..., 14]` with 0, 1 and 2 doing the IO.
RankAssignmentMode.label: Rank Assignment Mode

RankAssignmentMode.description: When **NumberOfIORanks** is greater than 1 and less than the number of MPI ranks, this controls how the ranks that write to disk are determined. This also affects which ranks send data to which rank for IO. In **Contiguous** mode (default), all MPI ranks are numerically grouped into **NumberOfIORanks** groups with the first rank in each group acting as the `root` node for that group and is the one that does IO. For example, if there are 16 MPI ranks and NumberOfIORanks is set to 3 then the groups are `[0 - 5], [6 - 10], [11 - 15]` with the first rank in each group 0, 6, and 15 doing the IO. In **RoundRobin** mode, the grouping is done in round robin fashion, thus for 16 MPI ranks with NumberOfIORanks set to 3, the groups are `[0, 3, ..., 15], [1, 4, ..., 13], [2, 5, ..., 14]` with 0, 1 and 2 doing the IO.
